sentences.zh: 安平獻王孚

translations.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.

sentences.zh: 安平獻王孚，字叔達，宣帝次弟也。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu, courtesy name Shuda, was Emperor Xuan's next younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Fu, Prince Xian of Anping, styled Shuda, was the younger brother who followed Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi).

sentences.zh: 初，孚長兄朗字伯達，宣帝字仲達，孚弟馗字季達，恂字顯達，進字惠達，通字雅達，敏字幼達，俱知名，故時號為「八達」焉。

translations.literal: At first Fu's eldest brother Lang had courtesy name Boda; Emperor Xuan had courtesy name Zhongda; Fu's younger brothers were Kui, courtesy Jida; Xun, Xiangda; Jin, Huida; Tong, Yada; and Min, Youda; all were renowned, so people at the time called them the 'Eight Worthies.'
translations.idiomatic: The brothers—Lang (Boda), Emperor Xuan as Zhongda, then Fu, Kui (Jida), Xun (Xiangda), Jin (Huida), Tong (Yada), and Min (Youda)—were famous across the land and folk dubbed them the 'Eight Worthies.'

sentences.zh: 孚溫厚廉讓，博涉經史。

translations.literal: Fu was warm and generous, honest and yielding, and broadly read the Classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Warm, modest, and widely read in classical texts and history, he carried himself with unassuming grace.

sentences.zh: 漢末喪亂，與兄弟處危亡之中，簞食瓢飲，而披閱不倦。

translations.literal: At the end of the Han there was turmoil and disorder; with his brothers he dwelt amid peril and extinction, eating from bamboo baskets and drinking from gourd dippers, yet he wearied not of reading.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Han collapse he and his brothers lived on the verge of ruin on the plainest fare, yet he never tired of his books.

sentences.zh: 性通恕，以貞白自立，未嘗有怨於人。

translations.literal: By nature he was open and forgiving; by purity and integrity he established himself, and he never harbored resentment toward anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Forgiving by temperament and upright in reputation, he kept himself blameless and bore no grudges.

sentences.zh: 陳留殷武有名於海內，嘗罹罪譴，孚往省之，遂與同處分食，談者稱焉。

translations.literal: Yin Wu of Chenliu had renown throughout the realm; he once suffered condemnation for an offense. Fu went to visit him and shared lodging and divided food with him; those who spoke of it praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Wu of Chenliu—a man celebrated empire-wide—was censured and punished, Fu called on him and stayed to share quarters and meals; observers admired his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 魏陳思王植有俊才，清選官屬，以孚為文學掾。

translations.literal: Prince Si of Chen of Wei, Cao Zhi, had outstanding talent; in cleanly selecting officials he appointed Fu as literary aide.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi, Wei Prince Si of Chen, culled his staff for excellence and named Fu literary adjutant.

sentences.zh: 植負才陵物，孚每切諫，初不合意，後乃謝之。

translations.literal: Zhi relied on his talent and looked down on others; Fu often remonstrated sternly. At first this did not suit Zhi's wishes, but afterward Zhi apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi's brilliance made him imperious; Fu rebuked him sharply until, though initially offended, Cao Zhi came to apologize.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Grandee for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝崩，太子號哭過甚，孚諫曰：「大行晏駕，天下恃殿下為命。

translations.literal: When Wei Emperor Wu died, the heir apparent wailed excessively in grief. Fu remonstrated, saying, 'The late emperor has passed away; the realm depends upon Your Highness as its lifeline.'
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao died the crown prince gave way to prolonged lamentation. Fu urged him: 'The sovereign has left the world; the empire now waits on your word alone.'

sentences.zh: 當上為宗廟，下為萬國，奈何效匹夫之孝乎！

translations.literal: Above you must serve the ancestral temple; below you must serve the myriad states—how can you imitate the filial piety of a common man!
translations.idiomatic: Your duty reaches upward to the dynastic altars and downward to every principality—this is no time to indulge grief like an ordinary son.

sentences.zh: 」太子良久乃止，曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: The heir apparent after a long while stopped and said, 'What you say is right.'
translations.idiomatic: The heir fell silent a long moment, mastered himself, and answered, 'You speak truly.'

sentences.zh: 」時群臣初聞帝崩，相聚號哭，無復行列。

translations.literal: At that time when the ministers first heard the emperor had died, they gathered together and wailed; there was no longer any order of ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The officials, thunderstruck by the news, had crowded together weeping without discipline or formation.

sentences.zh: 孚厲聲於朝曰：「今大行晏駕，天下震動，當早拜嗣君，以鎮海內，而但哭邪！

translations.literal: Fu thundered in court: 'Now the late emperor has passed away and the realm is shaken; we should promptly install the successor to stabilize the realm within the seas—and yet you only weep!'
translations.idiomatic: Fu's voice cut across the hall: 'The throne stands empty and the realm trembles—we must seat the new ruler at once to calm the empire, not dissolve in tears!

sentences.zh: 」孚與尚書和洽罷群臣，備禁衛，具喪事，奉太子以即位，是為文帝。

translations.literal: Fu together with Minister of Writing He Qia dismissed the assembled ministers, prepared the palace guards, arranged the funeral observances, and presented the heir apparent to assume the throne—this was Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: With Minister He Qia he dispersed the disorderly crowd, secured the palace guard, ordered the obsequies, and invested the crown prince, who ascended as Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 時當選侍中、常侍等官，太子左右舊人頗諷諭主者，便欲就用，不調餘人。

translations.literal: At that time when selecting Palace Attendants and Regular Attendants and such offices, the heir apparent's former intimates largely hinted to those in charge that they wished to be appointed at once without transferring others.
translations.idiomatic: When posts such as palace attendant were to be filled, the prince's old companions leaned on the selectors to secure their own appointments and shut out outsiders.

sentences.zh: 孚曰：「雖有堯舜，必有稷契。

translations.literal: Fu said, 'Though there be Yao and Shun, there must still be Ji and Xie.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu objected: 'Even under Yao and Shun one still needed ministers like Ji and Xie.'

sentences.zh: 今嗣君新立，當進用海內英賢，猶患不得，如何欲因際會自相薦舉邪！

translations.literal: Now the successor has newly been established; we ought to advance and employ worthy men from within the realm—we still fear we cannot obtain enough; how can we wish to seize the occasion to recommend ourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Our new sovereign must draw on the empire's finest—we already worry the talent pool is thin; how dare cronies use the moment to nominate themselves?'

sentences.zh: 官失其任，得者亦不足貴。

translations.literal: If offices miss their proper appointments, even those who obtain them are not worth esteeming.
translations.idiomatic: Misplaced appointments cheapen every title, those who grab them included.

sentences.zh: 」遂更他選。

translations.literal: Thereupon they changed and made other selections.
translations.idiomatic: The slate was cleared and a fresh round of appointments chosen.

sentences.zh: 轉孚為中書郎、給事常侍，宿省內，除黃門侍郎，加騎都尉。

translations.literal: Fu was transferred to Palace Secretariat Gentleman and Serving Regular Attendant, lodged inside the palace overnight; he was appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman and additionally conferred Chief Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to secretariat attendant and duty regular attendant, billeted inside the palace; then yellow-gate gentleman with supernumerary chief commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時孫權稱籓，請送任子，當遣前將軍于禁還，久而不至。

translations.literal: At that time Sun Quan declared himself a vassal and requested to send a hostage son; it was intended to send back former general Yu Jin, but after a long time he still had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had submitted as a tributary and offered to send a royal hostage and return the captive Yu Jin—but neither pledge appeared.

sentences.zh: 天子以問孚，孚曰：「先王設九服之制，誠以要荒難以德懷，不以諸夏禮責也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven asked Fu about it. Fu said, 'The former kings established the nine domains system—truly because the distant and wild regions are hard to win by virtue alone, and they did not hold them to Central States ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Fu, who replied: 'The ancient ninefold division assumed border peoples resist moral suasion alone—you cannot demand court etiquette of them as you would of the heartland.'

sentences.zh: 陛下承緒，遠人率貢。

translations.literal: Your Majesty carries on the succession; distant peoples all come bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under your reign distant peoples already stream in with tribute.

sentences.zh: 權雖未送任子，於禁不至，猶宜以寬待之，畜養士馬，以觀其變。

translations.literal: Though Quan has not yet sent the hostage son and Yu Jin has not arrived, still it is fitting to treat him generously, nurture soldiers and horses, and observe how matters change.
translations.idiomatic: Though Sun Quan withholds his son and Yu Jin lingers, patience still serves—feed your armies and watch how the wind shifts.

sentences.zh: 不可以嫌疑責讓，恐傷懷遠之義。

translations.literal: One must not on account of suspicion reproach and blame him, lest one wound the principle of cherishing those far away.
translations.idiomatic: Do not nag him with suspicion or you will spoil the policy of winning distant allegiance.

sentences.zh: 自孫策至權，奕世相繼，惟強與弱，不在一禁，禁之未至，當有他故耳。

translations.literal: From Sun Ce down to Quan, generations succeed one another; strength and weakness lie not in one Yu Jin; when Jin does not arrive, there ought to be another reason.
translations.idiomatic: From Sun Ce to Sun Quan the house endures by force of arms; Yu Jin is hardly the linchpin—if he tarries, some other cause explains it.

sentences.zh: 」後禁至，果以疾遲留，而任子竟不至。

translations.literal: Afterward Jin arrived; indeed he had delayed because of illness, yet in the end the hostage son never came.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin eventually appeared, detained by illness as Fu predicted, yet the hostage never followed.

sentences.zh: 大軍臨江，責其違言，吳遂絕不貢獻。

translations.literal: When the great army reached the Yangzi they blamed Wu for breaking its word, and Wu then utterly ceased tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Once imperial troops stood on the river and challenged Wu's breach of faith, tribute from the south stopped altogether.

sentences.zh: 後出為河內典農，賜爵關內侯，轉清河太守。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Agrarian Director for Henei, was enfeoffed with rank of district marquis within the passes, and transferred to governor of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Henei agrarian director, received a secondary marquisate within the passes, then governed Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 初，魏文帝置度支尚書，專掌軍國支計，朝議以征討未息，動須節量。

translations.literal: At first Wei Emperor Wen established the Minister of Revenue to specialize in army and state expenditures; court discussion held that with expeditions still unfinished, movements constantly required moderation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had created the revenue ministry for military supply; court opinion stressed ongoing campaigns meant every outlay needed restraint.

sentences.zh: 及明帝嗣位，欲用孚，問左右曰：「有兄風不？

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming succeeded the throne he wished to employ Fu and asked those around him, 'Does he have his elder brother's manner?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne he meant to promote Fu and asked his attendants whether the man matched his brother's caliber.

sentences.zh: 」答云：「似兄。

translations.literal: They answered, saying, 'He resembles his elder brother.'
translations.idiomatic: They answered that he did resemble Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 」天子曰：「吾得司馬懿二人，復何憂哉！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven said, 'If I obtain two Sima Yis, what else need I worry about!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, 'Two Sima Yis at court—and what trouble could remain?'

sentences.zh: 」轉為度支尚書。

translations.literal: Fu was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was named minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 孚以為擒敵制勝，宜有備預。

translations.literal: Fu held that to seize the enemy and achieve victory there ought to be preparedness beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Fu insisted victory required planning ahead.

sentences.zh: 每諸葛亮入寇關中，邊兵不能制敵，中軍奔赴，輒不及事機，宜預選步騎二萬，以為二部，為討賊之備。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhuge Liang invaded Guanzhong, the frontier troops could not check the enemy and the central army rushed to the rescue but always missed the moment; he proposed beforehand to select twenty thousand infantry and cavalry and divide them into two corps as preparations for punishing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Zhuge Liang struck Guanzhong the border garrisons buckled while reinforcements arrived too late; Fu urged standing two corps of twenty thousand foot and horse in readiness.

sentences.zh: 又以關中連遭賊寇，穀帛不足，遣冀州農丁五千屯於上邽，秋冬習戰陣，春夏修田桑。

translations.literal: Also because Guanzhong had repeatedly suffered bandit raids and grain and silk were insufficient, he sent five thousand farming households from Ji Province to garrison Shanggui; in autumn and winter they drilled battle formations, in spring and summer they tended fields and mulberries.
translations.idiomatic: With Guanzhong stripped by raids and short of grain and cloth, he relocated five thousand Ji cultivators to Shanggui to drill in winter and farm in summer.

sentences.zh: 由是關中軍國有餘，待賊有備矣。

translations.literal: By this means Guanzhong's army and state had surplus and awaited the enemy prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The western theater grew solvent while keeping the foe under watch.

sentences.zh: 後除尚書右僕射，進爵昌平亭侯，遷尚書令。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, advanced in rank to Marquis of Changping precinct, and promoted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice director of the secretariat, marquis of Changping ting, then director.

sentences.zh: 及大將軍曹爽擅權，李勝、何晏、鄧颺等亂政，孚不視庶事，但正身遠害而已。

translations.literal: When Grand General Cao Shuang monopolized power and Li Sheng, He Yan, Deng Yang, and others threw government into chaos, Fu did not attend to routine affairs but simply corrected himself and kept distant from harm.
translations.idiomatic: Under Cao Shuang's dictatorship and the cabal of Li Sheng, He Yan, and Deng Yang, Fu withdrew from daily administration and merely kept his head down.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝誅爽，孚與景帝屯司馬門，以功進爵長社縣侯，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan executed Shuang, Fu together with Emperor Jing held Sima Gate; by merit he advanced to marquis of Changshe county and was additionally appointed palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi struck down Shuang, Fu and Sima Shi sealed Sima Gate; for that service he became marquis of Changshe and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時吳將諸葛恪圍新城，以孚進督諸軍二十萬防禦之。

translations.literal: At that time Wu general Zhuge Ke besieged Xincheng; Fu was promoted to supervise two hundred thousand troops of all armies in defense.
translations.idiomatic: As Wu's Zhuge Ke pressed Xincheng, Fu took overall command of two hundred thousand defenders.

sentences.zh: 孚次壽春，遣毌丘儉、文欽等進討。

translations.literal: Fu halted at Shouchun and dispatched Guanqiu Jian, Wen Qin, and others to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: He camped at Shouchun and sent Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin forward.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲速擊之，孚曰：「夫攻者，借人之力以為功，且當詐巧，不可力爭也。

translations.literal: The generals wished to strike quickly; Fu said, 'In attacking, one borrows others' strength to accomplish merit, and moreover ought to rely on stratagem and cunning—one cannot contend by brute force.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates clamored for a hasty blow; Fu answered that assault borrows the enemy's strength and demands craft, not a frontal shoving match.'

sentences.zh: 」故稽留月餘乃進軍，吳師望風而退。

translations.literal: Therefore he delayed over a month before advancing the army, and the Wu army withdrew at the rumor of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: He waited more than a month before marching, and the Wu host melted away at the news.

sentences.zh: 魏明悼後崩，議書銘旌，或欲去姓而書魏，或欲兩書，孚以為：「經典正義，皆不應書。

translations.literal: When Wei Empress Mingdao died, discussion turned to the funeral banner inscription; some wished to omit the surname and write only Wei, some wished to write both; Fu held that canonical glosses alike say neither should be written.
translations.idiomatic: Debating the mortuary banner after Empress Mingdao's death, some wanted 'Wei' alone or surname plus title; Fu cited classical commentary against both.

sentences.zh: 凡帝王皆因本國之名以為天下之號，而與往代相別耳，非為擇美名以自光也。

translations.literal: In general emperors all take their state's name as the title for All Under Heaven in order to distinguish themselves from former dynasties; it is not that they choose a pretty name to glorify themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereigns style All Under Heaven after their house to mark the succession—not to mint flattering slogans.

sentences.zh: 天稱皇天，則帝稱皇帝，地稱后土，則後稱皇后。

translations.literal: Heaven is called August Heaven, then the emperor is called August Emperor; earth is called sovereign earth, then the empress is called August Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Heaven is 'August Heaven,' so the ruler is 'August Emperor'; earth is 'sovereign soil,' the consort 'August Empress.'

sentences.zh: 此乃所以同天地之大號，流無二之尊名，不待稱國號以自表，不俟稱氏族以自彰。

translations.literal: This is how they share heaven and earth's great titles and spread an unrivaled honorific name—they need not add the state's name to distinguish themselves nor wait to declare clan surname to display themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they pair cosmic titles with singular dignity without appending dynastic labels or clan names.

sentences.zh: 是以《春秋》隱公三年《經》曰'三月庚戌天王崩'，尊而稱天，不曰周王者，所以殊乎列國之君也。

translations.literal: Therefore in Duke Yin's third year the Classic records 'In the third month, on gengxu, the August Heaven King died,' honoring him by calling him Heaven and not saying King of Zhou in order to distinguish him from the lords of the states.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Spring and Autumn records 'the August Heaven died'—not 'Zhou king'—to set him above feudal rulers.

sentences.zh: '八月庚辰宋公和卒'，書國稱名，所以異乎天王也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengchen, Duke He of Song died—recording the state and personal name distinguishes him from the August Heaven King.
translations.idiomatic: 'Duke He of Song died' names state and man to contrast with the celestial ruler.

sentences.zh: 襄公十五年《經》曰'劉夏逆王后于齊'，不雲逆周王后姜氏者，所以異乎列國之夫人也。

translations.literal: In Duke Xiang's fifteenth year the Classic says 'Liu Xia meets the queen consort at Qi' without saying he meets the Zhou queen consort Jiang—thereby distinguishing her from the wives of the states.
translations.idiomatic: 'Liu Xia meets the queen at Qi' omits Zhou and Jiang to keep the royal consort apart from duchesses.

sentences.zh: 至乎列國，則曰'夫人姜氏至自齊'，又曰'紀伯姬卒'，書國稱姓，此所以異乎天王後也。

translations.literal: As for the states it says 'Lady Jiang arrived from Qi' and also says 'Bo Ji of Ji died'—recording state and surname distinguishes them from the August Heaven's queen.
translations.idiomatic: For feudal ladies the text gives state and clan to separate them from the Son of Heaven's wife.'

sentences.zh: 由此考之，尊稱皇帝，赫赫無二，何待魏乎？

translations.literal: Examining this, the honored title August Emperor shines unrivaled—why add Wei?
translations.idiomatic: If 'August Emperor' already towers alone, what need for 'Wei'?

sentences.zh: 尊稱皇后，彰以諡號，何待於姓乎？

translations.literal: The honored title August Empress is displayed by posthumous title—why wait for the surname?
translations.idiomatic: If 'August Empress' carries her epithet, why tack on a surname?

sentences.zh: 議者欲書魏者，此以為天皇之尊，同于往古列國之君也。

translations.literal: Those who argue for writing Wei treat the celestial emperor's honor as equal to the feudal lords of old.
translations.idiomatic: Advocates of writing 'Wei' reduce the sovereign to a mere feudal chief.

sentences.zh: 或欲書姓者，此以為天皇之後，同于往古之夫人也。

translations.literal: Those who argue for writing the surname treat the celestial consort as equal to the wives of old.
translations.idiomatic: Advocates of adding surnames liken the empress to ordinary noblewomen.

sentences.zh: 乖經典之大義，異乎聖人之明制，非所以垂訓將來，為萬世不易之式者也。

translations.literal: They violate the great meaning of the Classics and differ from the sage's clear institutions—it is not something by which to instruct posterity or serve as an unchanging model for myriad generations.
translations.idiomatic: Both notions betray canonical intent and sage kings' precedent—no lesson for later ages or eternal formula.'

sentences.zh: 」遂從孚議。

translations.literal: Thereupon they followed Fu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Fu's reading.

sentences.zh: 遷司空。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of works.

sentences.zh: 代王淩太尉。

translations.literal: He succeeded Wang Ling as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Wang Ling as grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 及蜀將-{姜}-維寇隴右，雍州刺史王經戰敗，遣孚西鎮關中，統諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Shu general Jiang Wei raided Longyou, Inspector of Yong Province Wang Jing was defeated in battle; Fu was dispatched west to secure Guanzhong and command all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Wei struck Longyou and Yong inspector Wang Jing collapsed, Fu went west to steady Guanzhong with supreme command.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍陳泰與安西將軍鄧艾進擊維，維退。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West Chen Tai and General Who Pacifies the West Deng Ai advanced and attacked Jiang Wei, and Jiang Wei withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai and Deng Ai drove Jiang Wei back.

sentences.zh: 孚還京師，轉太傅。

translations.literal: Fu returned to the capital and was transferred to Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 及高貴鄉公遭害，百官莫敢奔赴，孚枕屍於股，哭之慟，曰：「殺陛下者臣之罪。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang suffered violent death, none of the hundred officials dared go to the scene; Fu pillowed the corpse on his thigh, wept bitterly, and said, 'Those who killed Your Majesty are my crime.'
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Mao's murder officials shrank away; Fu cradled the body, sobbed, and cried that his own failure had killed the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 」奏推主者。

translations.literal: He memorialized to pursue those responsible.
translations.idiomatic: He filed charges against the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 會太后令以庶人禮葬，孚與群公上表，乞以王禮葬，從之。

translations.literal: When it happened that the empress dowager ordered burial by commoner rites, Fu together with the dukes submitted a memorial begging burial by princely rites; she assented.
translations.idiomatic: Though the empress dowager first demanded a commoner's funeral, Fu and his peers petitioned for kingly honors and won consent.

sentences.zh: 孚性至慎。

translations.literal: Fu's nature was extremely cautious.
translations.idiomatic: By temperament he was exceedingly careful.

sentences.zh: 宣帝執政，常自退損。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan held power he often withdrew and diminished himself.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sima Yi's supremacy he habitually effaced himself.

sentences.zh: 後逢廢立之際，未嘗預謀。

translations.literal: Later when occasions of deposition and enthronement came, he never participated in plotting.
translations.idiomatic: At every coup and enthronement thereafter he kept clear of the plotting.

sentences.zh: 景文二帝以孚屬尊，不敢逼。

translations.literal: Emperors Jing and Wen, because Fu's standing was venerable, did not dare coerce him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao honored his seniority and never leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 後進封長樂公。

translations.literal: Later he was advanced and enfeoffed as duke of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He was later advanced to duke of Changle.

sentences.zh: 及武帝受禪，陳留王就金墉城，孚拜辭，執王手，流涕歔欷，不能自勝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, the king of Chenliu went to Jinyong Fortress; Fu took leave of him, grasped the king's hand, wept and sobbed, and could not overcome himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne the Wei emperor withdrew to Jinyong; Fu clasped his hand in farewell and wept uncontrollably.

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣死之日，固大魏之純臣也。

translations.literal: He said, 'On the day I die I shall indeed be a pure minister of Great Wei.'
translations.idiomatic: 'When I die,' he vowed, 'I will still count myself Wei loyalist to the bone.'

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「太傅勳德弘茂，朕所瞻仰，以光導弘訓，鎮靜宇內，願奉以不臣之禮。

translations.literal: An edict said, 'The Grand Mentor's merit and virtue are vast and flourishing—what I look up to; by him brilliance guides instruction and calms the realm within the four seas—I wish to accord him rites that need not treat him as subject.
translations.idiomatic: The edict praised his towering virtue and offered him honors beyond subjecthood so his example might steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 其封為安平王，邑四萬戶。

translations.literal: Enfeoff him as prince of Anping with forty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was created prince of Anping at forty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 進拜太宰、持節、都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Advance him to Grand Preceptor, bearer of credentials, and commander-in-chief of all military affairs inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions followed: grand preceptor, credential-bearing commander of armies court-wide.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏，諸王未之國者，所置官屬，權未有備。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that for princes not yet gone to their fiefs the assigned staffs still lacked full appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaus noted princes remaining at capital lacked complete households.

sentences.zh: 帝以孚明德屬尊，當宣化樹教，為群後作則，遂備置官屬焉。

translations.literal: The emperor held that Fu's bright virtue and eminent standing ought to propagate transformation and establish instruction and serve as model for the host of kings; thereupon full staffs were completely appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled Fu's moral weight required a full household to model conduct for other royal uncles.

sentences.zh: 又以孚內有親戚，外有交遊，惠下之費，而經用不豐，奉絹二千匹。

translations.literal: Also because Fu had relatives within and friends without and expenses in showing kindness to subordinates yet regular income was not abundant, he was granted two thousand bolts of tribute silk.
translations.idiomatic: Considering his kin, his hospitality, and modest stipend, the throne added two thousand rolls of silk.

sentences.zh: 及元會，詔孚輿車上殿，帝於阼階迎拜。

translations.literal: At the New Year audience an edict ordered Fu's carriage onto the hall while the emperor greeted him with a bow on the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: At court assembly his cart mounted the hall while Sima Yan bowed him in from the eastern stair.

sentences.zh: 既坐，帝親奉觴上壽，如家人禮。

translations.literal: Once seated the emperor personally raised a cup and toasted him with family courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Seated, the emperor toasted him with familial warmth.

sentences.zh: 帝每拜，孚跪而止之。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor bowed, Fu knelt to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Sima Yan bowed, Fu dropped to his knees to forbid it.

sentences.zh: 又給以雲母輦、青蓋車。

translations.literal: He was also granted a mica-canopied carriage and a blue-canopied coach.
translations.idiomatic: He received a mica litter and an azure parasol carriage.

sentences.zh: 孚雖見尊寵，不以為榮，常有憂色。

translations.literal: Though Fu saw honor and favor he did not regard it as glory and often wore a troubled expression.
translations.idiomatic: Yet privilege brought him no joy—his face stayed shadowed with worry.

sentences.zh: 臨終，遺令曰：「有魏貞士河內溫縣司馬孚，字叔達，不伊不周，不夷不惠，立身行道，終始若一，當以素棺單槨，斂以時服。

translations.literal: At his deathbed his testament said, 'There was a Wei loyalist of Henei Wen county, Sima Fu, courtesy Shuda—not acting Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou, neither withdrawing like Boyi nor compromising like Liuxiahui—who established himself and walked the Way from first to last as one; bury me in an unvarnished coffin with a single-layer outer shell and dress me in timely ordinary clothes.'
translations.idiomatic: His dying charge styled himself Wei's steadfast servant from Wen county—no regent's ambition, no hermit's retreat—consistent lifelong; he demanded plain inner and outer coffins and everyday burial dress.'

sentences.zh: 」薨，時年九十三。

translations.literal: He died at age ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 帝於太極東堂舉哀三日。

translations.literal: The emperor observed mourning three days in the eastern hall of Taiji Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu mourned three days in Taiji's east hall.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「王勳德超世，尊寵無二，期頤在位，朕之所倚。

translations.literal: An edict said, 'The prince's merit and virtue surpass the age; honor and favor were without peer; he dwelt in office at a hundred years—what I relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The edict mourned a peerless pillar who had outlived a century on whom the throne leaned.

sentences.zh: 庶永百齡，諮仰訓導，奄忽殂隕，哀慕感切。

translations.literal: I hoped he would last forever to consult and look up to his instruction—suddenly he has fallen and passed away; grief and longing cut deep.
translations.idiomatic: I expected endless counsel; his sudden loss leaves desolate grief.

sentences.zh: 其以東園溫明秘器、朝服一具、衣一襲、緋練百匹、絹布各五百匹、錢百萬，穀千斛以供喪事。

translations.literal: Let there be supplied for the funeral the eastern park warming coffin and secret fittings, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, one hundred bolts of crimson silk, five hundred bolts each of silk and cloth, a million cash, and a thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Obsequies were to include imperial mortuary gear, court robes, grave clothes, crimson and plain silks, cash, and grain per statute.

sentences.zh: 諸所施行，皆依漢東平獻王蒼故事。

translations.literal: All measures implemented shall follow the precedent of Han Prince Xian of Dongping, Liu Cang.
translations.idiomatic: Rites followed Han Prince Xian of Dongping's precedent.'

sentences.zh: 」其家遵孚遺旨，所給器物，一不施用。

translations.literal: His family obeyed Fu's testamentary instructions; not one of the supplied implements was used.
translations.idiomatic: The clan honored his will and refused every gifted token.

sentences.zh: 帝再臨喪，親拜盡哀。

translations.literal: The emperor twice attended the mourning and personally bowed in full grief.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan returned twice to bow in deepest sorrow.

sentences.zh: 及葬，又幸都亭，望柩而拜，哀動左右。

translations.literal: When it came to burial he also went to the courier station, gazed toward the bier and bowed, moving those around him to grief.
translations.idiomatic: At interment he halted at the post station, bowed toward the catafalque, and moved every witness.

sentences.zh: 給鑾輅輕車，介士武賁百人，吉凶導從二千餘人，前後鼓吹，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: There were provided imperial escort carriages and light wagons, one hundred armored guards and palace runners, over two thousand attendants for auspicious and inauspicious processions, front and rear trumpets and drums, and joint sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The cortège drew imperial hearses, a hundred household guards, two thousand ushers, full musical escort, and enshrinement beside the royal ancestors.

sentences.zh: 九子：邕、望、輔、翼、晃、瑰、珪、衡、景。

translations.literal: Nine sons: Yong, Wang, Fu, Yi, Huang, Gui (lapis), Gui (jade tablet), Heng, Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons named Yong, Wang, Fu, Yi, Huang, Gui, Gui, Heng, and Jing—the fifth and sixth homophonous but written with different graphs.

translations.literal: Zi Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The heir, Yong.

sentences.zh: =邕字子魁。

translations.literal: Yong styled Zikui (the leading equals sign is a table marker in the source).
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong bore the courtesy name Zikui.

sentences.zh: 初為世子，拜步兵校尉、侍中。

translations.literal: At first he was heir apparent and was appointed Colonel of Infantry and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: While heir he served as colonel of infantry and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 先孚卒，追贈輔國將軍，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died before Fu; posthumously he was invested Assistant-General Who Supports the State with posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He predeceased Sima Fu and was posthumously named assistant general who supports the state, with the epithet Zhen.

sentences.zh: 邕子崇為世孫，又早夭。

translations.literal: Yong's son Chong was heir grandson and also died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong was named next-generation heir but died in childhood.

sentences.zh: ，立崇弟平陽亭侯隆為安平王。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chong's younger brother Long, Marquis of Pingyang precinct, was established as prince of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then invested Chong's younger brother Long—marquis of Pingyang ting—as Prince of Anping.

sentences.zh: 立四年，薨，諡曰穆，無子，國絕。

translations.literal: After four years on the throne he died; posthumous title was Mu; having no son, the state was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he died with epithet Mu; without heirs the principality was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 邕弟義陽成王望

translations.literal: Yong's younger brother Wang, Prince Cheng of Yiyang
translations.idiomatic: Yong's brother Sima Wang, Prince Cheng of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: =義陽成王望，字子初，出繼伯父朗，寬厚有父風。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Yiyang, Wang, courtesy Zichu, went out to succeed uncle Lang; he was generous and mild and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wang, Prince Cheng of Yiyang, styled Zichu, was adopted into uncle Sima Lang's line—open-handed and steady like his father.

sentences.zh: 仕郡上計吏，舉孝廉，辟司徒掾，曆平陽太守、洛陽典農中郎將。

translations.literal: He served the commandery as accounts clerk, was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, was summoned as aide to the Minister of Education, and successively held governor of Pingyang and Agrarian Commandant of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from commandery accountant through filial-incorrupt recommendation and ministerial aide to Pingyang governor and Luoyang agrarian colonel.

sentences.zh: 從宣帝討王淩，以功封永安亭侯。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xuan to punish Wang Ling and by merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Yong'an precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning with Sima Yi against Wang Ling earned him the Yong'an ting marquisate.

sentences.zh: 遷護軍將軍，改封安樂鄉侯，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Guards the Army, changed enfeoffment to Marquis of Anle village, and added irregular cavalry attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted general who guards the army, he exchanged his fief for Anle township and received supernumerary cavalry attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 時魏高貴鄉公好才愛士，望與裴秀、王沈、鍾會並見親待，數侍宴筵。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Duke of Gaoguixiang loved talent and cherished scholars; Wang together with Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, and Zhong Hui alike saw intimate favor and repeatedly attended banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mao cultivated writers and thinkers; Wang joined Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, and Zhong Hui in the emperor's intimate circle at countless banquets.

sentences.zh: 公性急，秀等居內職，急有召便至。

translations.literal: The duke was impatient by nature; Xiu and others held inner posts and when urgently summoned arrived at once.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's temper ran hot; men like Pei Xiu, holding palace posts, could answer an urgent summons immediately.

sentences.zh: 以望外官，特給追鋒車一乘，武賁五人。

translations.literal: Because Wang was an outer official, specially there was given one swift-response carriage and five palace runners.
translations.idiomatic: As an outsider he was granted a rapid courier cart and five household guards.

sentences.zh: 時景文相繼輔政，未嘗朝覲，權歸晉室。

translations.literal: At that time Jing and Wen succeeded each other as regents and never held court audience; power returned to the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao ruled behind the curtain without formal audiences—effective authority already rested with the future Jin house.

sentences.zh: 望雖見寵待，每不自安，由是求出，為征西將軍、持節、都督雍涼二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Though Wang saw favor and treatment, often he was not at ease; on this account he sought to go out and became General Who Conquers the West, bearer of credentials, and supervisor of all military affairs of Yong and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Royal favor could not settle him; he won a western command as conquering-general with credentials over Yong and Liang.

sentences.zh: 在任八年，威化明肅。

translations.literal: In office eight years, his awe-inspiring transformation was bright and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Across eight years his governance ran lucid and austere.

sentences.zh: 先是蜀將薑維屢寇關中，及望至，廣設方略，維不得為寇，關中賴之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shu general Jiang Wei repeatedly raided Guanzhong; when Wang arrived he broadly laid plans and measures so Wei could not raid; Guanzhong relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Wei's repeated strikes on Guanzhong, Wang's strategy stopped further incursions and steadied the northwest.

sentences.zh: 進封順陽侯。

translations.literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed Marquis of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: His fief rose to marquis of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 徵拜衛將軍，領中領軍，典禁兵。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed General Who Guards the Metropolis, concurrently Central Army Supervisor, in charge of palace troops.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as metropolitan guard, he headed the central army and commanded palace soldiers.

sentences.zh: 尋加驃騎將軍、開府。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Champion General and granted independent headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added champion-general rank with an independent staff.

sentences.zh: 頃之，代何曾為司徒。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced He Zeng as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he succeeded He Zeng as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封義陽王，邑萬戶，給兵二千人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Yiyang with ten thousand households and two thousand troops granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne Wang became prince of Yiyang at ten thousand households with a guard allotment of two thousand.

sentences.zh: ，詔曰：「夫尚賢庸勳，尊宗茂親，所以體國經化，式是百辟也。

translations.literal: An edict said, 'To esteem the worthy and employ the meritorious, to honor the clan and enrich kin—that is how one embodies the state and regulates transformation and serves as model for the hundred ministers.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed that lifting up talent and kinsmen stabilizes the altars and sets the tone for every minister.

sentences.zh: 且台司之重，存乎天官，故周建六職，政典為首。

translations.literal: Moreover the weight of the terrace ministers rests in Heaven's offices; therefore Zhou established six duties and governance statutes came first.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers mirror celestial offices—the Zhou six portfolios placed governance foremost.

sentences.zh: 司徒、中領軍，以明德近屬，世濟其美；

translations.literal: Minister of Education and Central Army Supervisor—by bright virtue as close kin across generations perfect their excellence;
translations.idiomatic: Your concurrent posts as minister of education and central-army supervisor marry imperial virtue with royal kinship.

sentences.zh: 祖考創業，翼佐大命，出典方任，入贊朝政，文德既著，武功宣暢。

translations.literal: Grandfather and father founded enterprise, assisted the great mandate, went out to administer regional duty, entered to assist court governance; civil virtue was already manifest, martial merit widely displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Your ancestors forged the enterprise within court and along the frontiers—renown in civil arts and arms alike.

sentences.zh: 逮朕嗣位，弼道惟明，宜登上司，兼統軍戎，內輔帝室，外隆威重，其進位太尉，中領軍如故。

translations.literal: Down to Our succeeding the throne you have aided the Way with clarity; fittingly mount the high minister and concurrently command the army—within assist the imperial house, without raise mighty awe; We advance your rank to Grand Commandant; Central Army Supervisor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Under Our reign your counsel stays lucid; take grand commandant while retaining central-army charge—steady the palace within, awe the realm without.

sentences.zh: 置太尉軍司一人，參軍事六人，騎司馬五人。

translations.literal: Establish one army aide to the Grand Commandant, six military staff advisers, five cavalry majors.
translations.idiomatic: Staff shall include one grand-commandant army director, six military advisers, and five cavalry majors.

sentences.zh: 又增置官騎十人，並前三十，假羽葆鼓吹。」

translations.literal: Also additionally establish ten official mounted escorts—together with the former thirty—and confer feather-canopy band and drum.
translations.idiomatic: Add ten mounted guards to the thirty already assigned, together with feathered canopy and ceremonial musicians.

sentences.zh: 吳將施績寇江夏，邊境騷動。

translations.literal: Wu general Shi Ji raided Jiangxia and the border was disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu general Shi Ji's strike on Jiangxia threw the frontier into alarm.

sentences.zh: 以望統中軍步騎二萬，出屯龍陂，為二方重鎮，假節，加大都督諸軍事。

translations.literal: Wang was ordered to command twenty thousand infantry and cavalry of the central army, go out and encamp at Longpi as heavy garrison for two fronts, given credentials, and additionally promoted grand commander of all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang led twenty thousand central troops to Longpi as the brace between two theaters, credentials in hand as grand commander.

sentences.zh: 會荊州刺史胡烈距績，破之，望乃班師。

translations.literal: It happened that Inspector of Jing Province Hu Lie resisted Ji and defeated him; thereupon Wang withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing inspector Hu Lie routed Shi Ji, Wang stood down his army.

sentences.zh: 俄而吳將丁奉寇芍陂，望又率諸軍以赴之，未至而奉退。

translations.literal: Soon Wu general Ding Feng raided Quepi; Wang again led the various armies to hurry there; before he arrived Feng withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng's raid on Quepi drew Wang east again, though the enemy slipped away before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 拜大司馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 孫皓率眾向壽春，詔望統中軍二萬，騎三千，據淮北。

translations.literal: Sun Hao led a host toward Shouchun; an edict ordered Wang to command twenty thousand central troops and three thousand cavalry and hold north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's thrust toward Shouchun sent Wang to the north bank of the Huai with twenty thousand foot and three thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 皓退，軍罷。

translations.literal: Hao withdrew and the army was disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao withdrew and the mobilization ended.

sentences.zh: 薨，時年六十七，賻贈有加，望性儉吝而好聚斂，身亡之後，金帛盈溢，以此獲譏。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-seven; funeral gifts were generous in addition; Wang's nature was frugal and stingy yet fond of amassing; after his death gold and silk overflowed; on this account he incurred ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven amid lavish obsequies yet earned ridicule for having hoarded treasure despite a miserly reputation.

sentences.zh: 四子：弈、洪、整、楙。

translations.literal: Four sons: Yi, Hong, Zheng, Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons survived him: Yi, Hong, Zheng, and Mao.

sentences.zh: 弈至黃門郎，先望卒。

translations.literal: Yi reached Yellow Gate Gentleman and died before Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi rose to yellow-gate gentleman but died before his father.

sentences.zh: 整亦早亡。

translations.literal: Zheng also died young.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng likewise died young.

sentences.zh: 以弈子奇襲爵。

translations.literal: By Yi's son Qi the noble rank was inherited.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to Yi's son Qi.

sentences.zh: 奇亦好畜聚，不知紀極，遣三部使到交廣商貨，為有司所奏，，詔貶為三縱亭侯。

translations.literal: Qi also loved to hoard and amass without knowing limit; he dispatched envoys of three bureaus to Jiao and Guang to trade goods and was memorialized by the relevant offices; an edict degraded him to Marquis of Sanzong precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Qi amassed wealth recklessly through trading missions until censored and demoted to marquis of Sanzong ting.

sentences.zh: 更以章武王威為望嗣。

translations.literal: Next Prince Wei of Zhangwu was made Wang's successor.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then named Sima Wei of Zhangwu as Wang's heir.

sentences.zh: 後威誅，復立奇為棘陽王以嗣望。

translations.literal: Later when Wei was executed, Qi was again established as Prince of Jiyang to succeed Wang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei's execution Qi was restored as Prince of Jiyang to continue Wang's line.

translations.idiomatic: Wang's son Sima Hong, Prince Ping of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 河間平王洪，字孔業，出繼叔父昌武亭侯遺。

translations.literal: Prince Ping of Hejian, Hong, courtesy Kongye, went out to succeed uncle Marquis of Changwu precinct Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Hong, Prince Ping of Hejian, styled Kongye, was adopted into uncle Yi's Changwu ting line.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，歷位典農中郎將、原武太守，封襄賁男。

translations.literal: Serving Wei he successively held Agrarian Commandant, governor of Yuanwu, and was enfeoffed Baron of Xiangben.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he served as agrarian colonel, Yuanwu governor, and baron of Xiangben.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封河間王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne Hong became prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 立十二年，薨。

translations.literal: Twelve years on the throne he died.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned twelve years and died.

sentences.zh: 二子：威、混。

translations.literal: Two sons: Wei and Hun.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons, Wei and Hun.

sentences.zh: 威嗣，徙封章武。

translations.literal: Wei succeeded and was transferred enfeoffment to Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei inherited and moved the fief to Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 其後威既繼義陽王望，更立混為洪嗣。

translations.literal: Later when Wei had succeeded Prince of Yiyang Wang, Hun was further established as Hong's successor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei continued Sima Wang's Yiyang title, Hun was designated Hong's heir.

sentences.zh: 混歷位散常侍，薨。

translations.literal: Hun successively held irregular attendant posts and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hun served as supernumerary cavalry attendant and died.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽陷，混諸子皆沒于胡。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell, Hun's various sons all fell captive among the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's fall sent Hun's sons into Hu captivity.

sentences.zh: 而小子滔初嗣新蔡王確，亦與其兄俱沒。

translations.literal: Yet the youngest son Tao had first succeeded Prince of Xincai Que and together with his elder brothers was also taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Youngest son Tao—even after succeeding Prince Que of Xincai—was seized alongside his brothers.

sentences.zh: 後得南還，與新蔡太妃不協。

translations.literal: Later obtaining southward return he was not harmonious with the Dowager Princess of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: After fleeing south he quarreled with his adoptive mother the Xincai dowager.

sentences.zh: 太興二年上疏，以兄弟並沒在遼東，章武國絕，宜還所生。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taixing he submitted a memorial stating that brothers alike were held captive in Liaodong, the Zhangwu state was cut off, and he ought to return to his birth family.
translations.idiomatic: In 319 he petitioned to return to his birth line while brothers remained in Liaodong and Zhangwu lacked heirs.

sentences.zh: 太妃訟之，事下太常。

translations.literal: The dowager princess sued him; the matter went down to the Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager sued; the court referred the case to the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 太常賀循議：「章武、新蔡俱承一國不絕之統，義不得替其本宗而先後傍親。

translations.literal: Minister He Xun argued: 'Zhangwu and Xincai alike inherit an unbroken mandate of one state; by principle one may not supplant one's root lineage for collateral kin out of order.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun held that both fiefs represent continuous succession—you cannot abandon your natural lineage for a collateral branch.

sentences.zh: 按滔既已被命為人後矣，必須無復兄弟，本國永絕，然後得還所生。

translations.literal: Accordingly Tao having already received appointment as someone's heir must wait until he certainly has no brothers left and his original state is forever cut off—only then may he return to those who bore him.
translations.idiomatic: An adoptee may revert only when no siblings survive and the native fief is truly extinct.

sentences.zh: 今兄弟在遠，不得言無，道里雖阻，復非絕域。

translations.literal: Now brothers are distant—one cannot say there are none; though roads are blocked they are again not unreachable wastes.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers still live beyond the frontier—hardly the vacuum that statute imagines.

sentences.zh: 且鮮卑恭命，信使不絕。

translations.literal: Moreover the Xianbei defer to commands; envoys do not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei still honor imperial summons—couriers move freely.

sentences.zh: 自宜詔下遼東，依劉群、盧諶等例，發遣令還，繼嗣本封。

translations.literal: Naturally it is fitting to issue edicts down to Liaodong following the precedent of Liu Qun, Lu Chen, and others, dispatch and order them to return and succeed their root enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: Order Liaodong to send them home under the Liu Qun and Lu Chen precedent so they may resume original titles.

sentences.zh: 謂滔今未得便委離所後也。

translations.literal: This means Tao now cannot conveniently abandon those he succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Tao cannot yet cast off his adoptive house.

sentences.zh: 」元帝詔曰：「滔雖出養，自有所生母。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan's edict said, 'Though Tao went out to be raised he naturally has a birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan replied that Tao still belonged by birth to his natural mother despite adoption.

sentences.zh: 新蔡太妃相待甚薄，滔執意如此。

translations.literal: The Dowager Princess of Xincai treated him very coldly; Tao held to his intent in this way.
translations.idiomatic: The Xincai dowager had treated him harshly; his determination to leave hardened.

sentences.zh: 如其不聽，終當紛紜，更為不可。

translations.literal: If she does not heed him in the end there will be wrangling and again it will be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing him to stay would invite endless litigation.

sentences.zh: 今便順其所執，還襲章武。」

translations.literal: Now let Us comply with what he insists on and let him return and inherit Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Grant his plea and restore him to the Zhangwu succession.

sentences.zh: 滔歷位散騎常侍，薨，子休嗣。

translations.literal: Tao successively held irregular cavalry attendant and died; son Xiu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tao rose to supernumerary cavalry attendant, died, and Xiu inherited.

sentences.zh: 休與彭城王雄俱奔蘇峻。

translations.literal: Xiu together with Prince Xiong of Pengcheng both fled to Su Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu fled with Prince Xiong of Pengcheng into Su Jun's camp.

sentences.zh: 峻平，休已戰死。

translations.literal: When Jun was pacified Xiu had already died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun fell Xiu was already slain on the field.

sentences.zh: 弟珍年八歲，以小弗坐。

translations.literal: Younger brother Zhen was eight years old and because young was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Eight-year-old Zhen escaped punishment as a minor.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，位至大宗正。

translations.literal: He inherited the noble rank and reached Grand Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the title and rose to director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 薨，無嗣，河間王欽以子範之繼，位至遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: He died without heir; Prince Qin of Hejian gave son Fan zhi to succeed; Fan zhi reached General Who Roams and Strikes.
translations.idiomatic: Without issue he was succeeded by Fan zhi, son of Prince Qin of Hejian—later promoted to roving-strike general.

sentences.zh: 薨，子秀嗣。

translations.literal: He died; son Xiu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Xiu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: ，為桂陽太守。

translations.literal: He became governor of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu governed Guiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 秀妻桓振之妹，振作逆，秀不自安，謀反，伏誅，國除。

translations.literal: Xiu's wife was Huan Zhen's younger sister; when Zhen rebelled Xiu was uneasy and plotted rebellion; he was executed by secret decree and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Married to Huan Zhen's sister, Xiu panicked when Zhen rebelled, plotted in turn, and was executed—the principality struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 洪子威

translations.literal: Hong zi Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Sima Wei.

sentences.zh: 威字景曜，初嗣洪。

translations.literal: Wei courtesy Jingyao at first succeeded Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wei, styled Jingyao, first inherited Hong.

sentences.zh: ，徙封章武。

translations.literal: He was transferred enfeoffment to Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was transferred to Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: ，嗣義陽王望。

translations.literal: He succeeded Prince of Yiyang Wang.
translations.idiomatic: He then continued Sima Wang's Yiyang princedom.

sentences.zh: 威凶暴無操行，諂附趙王倫。

translations.literal: Wei was fierce and violent without moral conduct and flattered and attached himself to Prince Zhao Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Savage and unscrupulous, he hitched himself to Sima Lun.

sentences.zh: 元康末，為散騎常侍，倫將篡，使威與黃門郎駱休逼帝奪璽綬，倫以威為中書令。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuankang he was irregular cavalry attendant; when Lun was about to usurp he sent Wei together with Yellow Gate Gentleman Luo Xiu to coerce the emperor and seize the seal cords; Lun appointed Wei Palace Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuankang he helped Sima Lun wrench the seal from Emperor Hui alongside Luo Xiu, then took the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 倫敗，惠帝反正，曰：「阿皮捩吾指，奪吾璽綬，不可不殺。

translations.literal: When Lun was defeated Emperor Hui resumed right rule and said, 'Api twisted my fingers and seized my seal cords—cannot fail to kill him.'
translations.idiomatic: After Lun collapsed Emperor Hui vowed to execute the cousin who had twisted his fingers off the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 」阿皮，威小字也。

translations.literal: Api was Wei's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: 'Api' was Wei's infant name.

sentences.zh: 於是誅威。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wei was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was put to death.

sentences.zh: 洪弟隨穆王整

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Zheng, Prince Mu of Sui
translations.idiomatic: Hong's brother Sima Zheng, Prince Mu of Sui.

sentences.zh: 隨穆王整，兄弈卒，以整為世子。

translations.literal: Prince Mu of Sui, Zheng—when elder brother Yi died Zheng was made heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died Zheng became heir of the Yiyang house.

sentences.zh: 曆南中郎將，封清泉侯，先父望薨，追贈冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He successively held General of the Southern Gentlemen, was enfeoffed Marquis of Qingquan; he died before his father Wang; when Wang died he was posthumously invested Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded southern gentlemen and held Qingquan marquis but predeceased Sima Wang; upon Wang's death the court posthumously named him Champion General.

sentences.zh: 武帝以義陽國一縣追封為隨縣王。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu used one county of the Yiyang state to posthumously enfeoff him as Prince of Sui county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu carved out Sui county from Yiyang for his posthumous princedom.

sentences.zh: 子邁嗣。

translations.literal: Son Mai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Mai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 太康九年，以義陽之平林益邁為隨郡王。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang Pinglin of Yiyang was added to enlarge Mai as Prince of Sui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 288 Yiyang's Pinglin canton enlarged Mai's domain to prince of Sui commandery.

sentences.zh: 整弟竟陵王楙

translations.literal: Zheng's younger brother Mao, Prince of Jingling
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's brother Sima Mao, prince of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王楙，字孔偉，初封樂陵亭侯，起家參相國軍事。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingling Mao, courtesy Kongwei, at first was enfeoffed Marquis of Leling precinct and began office as participant in princely-state military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mao, styled Kongwei, began as marquis of Leling ting on the prince's military staff.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封東平王，邑三千九十七戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Dongping with three thousand ninety-seven households.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan took the throne Mao became prince of Dongping at 3,097 households.

sentences.zh: 入為散騎常侍、尚書。

translations.literal: He entered court as irregular cavalry attendant and minister.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to the capital as supernumerary cavalry attendant and ministry counselor.

sentences.zh: 楙善諂諛，曲事楊駿。

translations.literal: Mao was skilled at flattery and fawning and bent his service to Yang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mao excelled at sycophancy and curried favor with Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 及駿誅，依法當死，東安公繇與楙善，故得不坐。

translations.literal: When Jun was executed, by law Mao ought to have died, but Duke of Dongan You was friendly with Mao, so he avoided punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's fall should have cost Mao his life, yet Sima You's friendship shielded him.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大鴻臚，加侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Grand Herald and added palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He soon rose to grand herald with supernumerary palace attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 繇欲擅朝政，與汝南王亮不平。

translations.literal: You wished to monopolize court government and was at odds with Prince Liang of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima You grasped for centralized power and clashed with Prince Liang of Runan.

sentences.zh: 帝托以繇討駿顧望，免繇、楙等官，遣楙就國。

translations.literal: The emperor on the pretext that You hesitated in attacking Jun removed You and Mao from office and sent Mao to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui blamed Sima You for half-hearted action against Jun, cashiered both men, and banished Mao to his domain.

sentences.zh: 楙殖財貨，奢僭逾制。

translations.literal: Mao amassed wealth and goods; extravagance and usurpation of ritual exceeded regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He hoarded treasure and flouted sumptuary law with pretensions beyond his rank.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫篡位，召還。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne he recalled Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun's coup brought Mao back to court.

sentences.zh: 及義兵起，倫以楙為衛將軍、都督諸軍事。

translations.literal: When the righteous host rose, Lun appointed Mao General Who Guards the Metropolis and supervisor of all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once loyalist armies rose Lun named Mao metropolitan guard and overall commander.

sentences.zh: 倫敗，楙免官。

translations.literal: When Lun was defeated Mao was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Lun's fall stripped Mao of his posts.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏輔政，繇復為僕射，舉楙為平東將軍、都督徐州諸軍事，鎮下邳。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Jiong assisted government You again became vice director and recommended Mao as General Who Pacifies the East and supervisor of Xu military affairs, stationed at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sima Jiong's regency Sima You returned as vice director and nominated Mao as pacifier-general for Xu based at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎輔政，進楙為衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Chengdu Ying assisted government Mao was advanced to General Who Guards the Metropolis.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying's turn at power promoted Mao to metropolitan guard.

sentences.zh: 會惠帝北征，即以楙為車騎將軍，都督如故，使率眾赴鄴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned north Mao was at once made chariot-and-cavalry general with supervisory duties unchanged and ordered to lead troops toward Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The northern expedition made Mao chariot-and-cavalry general at Ye with unchanged theater command.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之役，東海王越奔於下邳，楙不納，越乃還國。

translations.literal: In the Dangyin fighting Prince of Donghai Yue fled to Xiapi; Mao refused him entry, so Yue returned to his state.
translations.idiomatic: After Dangyin Sima Yue sought refuge at Xiapi; Mao shut the gates and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 帝既西幸，越總兵謀迎大駕，楙甚懼。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had fled west Yue gathered troops planning to welcome the imperial carriage; Mao was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Huiyi moved west Sima Yue mustered men to recover him; Mao panicked.

sentences.zh: 長史王修說曰：「東海宗室重望，今將興義，公宜舉徐州以授之，此克讓之美也。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Wang Xiu advised saying, 'Prince of Donghai carries heavy prestige among the imperial clan; now he will raise righteous arms—you ought to yield Xu Province to him; this is the beauty of yielding precedence.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu urged Mao to hand Xu to the eminent Sima Yue as the gracious move.

sentences.zh: 」楙從之，乃自承制都督兗州刺史、車騎將軍，表于天子。

translations.literal: Mao followed this; thereupon on his own authority under emergency regulations he acted as supervisor of Yan Province and chariot-and-cavalry general and memorialized the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mao complied, seized Yan under emergency orders as chariot-and-cavalry chief, and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時帝在長安，遣使者劉虔即拜焉。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was at Chang'an and dispatched envoy Liu Qian to confirm the appointment on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an the court sent Liu Qian to seal the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 楙慮兗州刺史苟晞不避己，乃給虔兵，使稱詔誅晞。

translations.literal: Mao feared Yan Inspector Gou Xi would not defer to him; therefore he supplied Qian troops and had him profess an edict executing Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Gou Xi, Mao armed Liu Qian with a forged warrant for Xi's death.

sentences.zh: 晞時已避位，楙在州徵求不已，郡縣不堪命。

translations.literal: Xi had already stepped aside, yet Mao in the province demanded endlessly; commanderies and counties could not bear the orders.
translations.idiomatic: Though Gou Xi had yielded, Mao's exactions broke the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 范陽王虓遣晞還兗州，徙楙都督青州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Fanyang sent Xi back to Yan Province and transferred Mao to supervise Qing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiao restored Gou Xi and shifted Mao to Qing theater.

sentences.zh: 楙不受命，背山東諸侯，與豫州刺史劉喬相結。

translations.literal: Mao refused the order, turned his back on the Shandong princes, and allied with Inspector Qiao of Yu Province Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Mao rejected the posting, broke with the eastern league, and joined Liu Qiao.

sentences.zh: 虓遣將田徽擊楙，破之，楙走還國。

translations.literal: Xiao dispatched general Tian Hui to strike Mao, defeated him, and Mao fled back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hui routed Mao, who bolted for his fief.

sentences.zh: 帝還洛陽，楙乃詣闕。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to Luoyang Mao then presented himself at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Once Luoyang welcomed Huiyi back Mao sued for entry.

sentences.zh: 及懷帝踐阼，改封竟陵王，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended he changed Mao's enfeoffment to Prince of Jingling and appointed Grand Master of Splendid Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Huai renamed him prince of Jingling and grand master of splendid horses.

sentences.zh: 越出牧豫州，留世子毗及其党何倫訪察宮省。

translations.literal: Yue went out as shepherd of Yu Province, leaving heir Pi and his faction He Lun to spy on the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue took Yu and left heir Pi and He Lun watching the inner court.

sentences.zh: 楙白帝討越，乃合眾襲倫，不克。

translations.literal: Mao informed the emperor to punish Yue; thereupon he gathered forces and attacked Lun but did not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao urged Huai to strike Yue, then struck He Lun and failed.

sentences.zh: 帝委罪於楙，楙奔竄獲免。

translations.literal: The emperor shifted blame onto Mao; Mao fled and escaped execution.
translations.idiomatic: Huai blamed Mao, who ran for his life.

sentences.zh: 越薨，乃出。

translations.literal: When Yue died he then emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Yue died did Mao surface.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽傾覆，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: When Luoyang collapsed he was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's fall left him slain by rogue soldiers.

sentences.zh: =望弟太原成王輔=

translations.literal: Wang di Taiyuan Cheng Wang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, Prince Cheng of Taiyuan—Sima Wang's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 太原成王輔，魏末為野王太守。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Taiyuan, Fu, at the end of Wei was governor of Yewang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wei Sima Fu governed Yewang.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封渤海王，邑五千三百七十九戶，之國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Bohai with five thousand three hundred seventy-nine households and proceeded to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan made him prince of Bohai at 5,379 households with orders to his domain.

sentences.zh: 後為衛尉，出為東中郎將，轉南中郎將，，徙為太原王，監并州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Later he was Commandant of the Guards, went out as General of the Eastern Gentlemen, transferred to General of the Southern Gentlemen, then was moved to Prince of Taiyuan supervising Bing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commandant of guards, eastern then southern gentleman-general, then Taiyuan prince commanding Bing.

sentences.zh: 入朝，五年薨，追贈鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: He entered court; in the fifth year he died and was posthumously invested General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to court he died in the fifth year of his reign with posthumous guard-north honors.

sentences.zh: ，更贈衛將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Moreover he was additionally posthumously invested General Who Guards the Metropolis with independent headquarters and ceremonies equal to the Three Lords.
translations.idiomatic: Later honors added metropolitan guard with full staff and three-dukes parity.

sentences.zh: 子弘立，元康中為散騎常侍，後徙封中丘王。

translations.literal: Son Hong succeeded; in Yuankang he was irregular cavalry attendant and later transferred enfeoffment to Prince of Zhongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Hong held supernumerary cavalry attendant then moved the title to Zhongqiu.

sentences.zh: 三年薨，子鑠立。

translations.literal: In the third year he died; son Shuo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Three years on Shuo inherited.

sentences.zh: =輔弟翼=

translations.literal: Fu di Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi—Fu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 翼字子世，少曆顯位，官至武賁中郎將。

translations.literal: Yi courtesy Zishi in youth successively held eminent posts and reached Major of the Household Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, styled Zishi, rose young to major among the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 武帝未受禪而卒，以兄邕之支子承為嗣，封南宮縣王。

translations.literal: Before Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he died; Yong's cadet son Cheng was appointed successor as Prince of Nangong county.
translations.idiomatic: He died before the Wei-Jin transition; Yong's collateral heir Cheng took Nangong county.

sentences.zh: 薨，子祐嗣立，承遂無後。

translations.literal: He died; son You succeeded and Cheng thereby had no posterity.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died You continued the line, ending Cheng's branch.

sentences.zh: =翼弟下邳獻王晃=

translations.literal: Yi di Xiapi Offering Wang Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, Prince Xian of Xiapi—Yi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 下邳獻王晃字子明，魏封武始亭侯，拜黃門侍郎，改封西安男，出為東莞太守。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Xiapi Huang courtesy Ziming was enfeoffed Marquis of Wushi precinct in Wei, appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman, changed to Baron of Xi'an, and went out as governor of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Huang, styled Ziming, began as Wushi ting marquis, yellow-gate gentleman, Xi'an baron, then Dongguan governor.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封下邳王，邑五千一百七十六戶，泰始二年就國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiapi with five thousand one hundred seventy-six households and proceeded to his state in Taishi year two.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan invested him at Xiapi with 5,176 households in 266.

sentences.zh: 晃孝友貞廉，謙虛下士，甚得宗室之稱。

translations.literal: Huang was filial, friendly, chaste, and honest, humble toward scholars, and greatly earned praise among the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Filial, modest, and scrupulous, he won wide esteem among kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 後為長水校尉、南中郎將。

translations.literal: Later he was Colonel of Long Waters and General of the Southern Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He later commanded long waters and southern gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔曰：「南中郎將、下邳王晃清亮中正，體行明潔，才周政理，有文武策識。

translations.literal: In the ninth year an edict said, 'Southern Gentlemen General Prince of Xiapi Huang is pure, bright, and upright; his conduct is lucid and clean; talent suffices for governance and he possesses civil and military stratagem.'
translations.idiomatic: A 273 edict praised Huang's clarity, integrity, and balanced civil-military talent.

sentences.zh: 其以晃為使持節，都督甯益二州諸軍事、安西將軍，領益州刺史。

translations.literal: Let Huang be credential-bearing commissioner supervising Ning and Yi military affairs, General Who Pacifies the West, and concurrently Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment made him credential-bearing pacifying-west general over Ning and Yi with concurrent Yi shepherd duties.

sentences.zh: 」晃以疾不行，更拜尚書，遷右僕射。

translations.literal: Huang pleaded illness and did not go; he was further appointed Minister of Writing and promoted Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Pleading illness he stayed north and instead took minister of writing and right vice director.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為鎮東將軍、都督青徐二州諸軍事。

translations.literal: After a long while he went out as General Who Guards the East supervising Qing and Xu military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he commanded Qing and Xu from the east.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，入為車騎將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended he entered as chariot-and-cavalry general with additional irregular cavalry attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hui made him chariot-and-cavalry chief with supernumerary cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 將誅楊駿，以晃領護軍，屯東掖門，尋守尚書令。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun was to be executed Huang was put in charge of the guards encamped at Dongye Gate and soon held Minister Director.
translations.idiomatic: During Yang Jun's purge he guarded Dongye Gate then acting minister director.

sentences.zh: 遷司空，加侍中，令如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted Minister of Works with additional palace attendant while retaining minister director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of works plus palace attendant, keeping director duties.

sentences.zh: 薨，追贈太傅。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously invested Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Death brought posthumous grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 二子：裒、綽。

translations.literal: Two sons: Pou and Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Pou and Chuo.

sentences.zh: 裒早卒，綽有篤疾，別封良城縣王，以太原王輔第三子韡為嗣。

translations.literal: Pou died early; Chuo had grave illness and separately was enfeoffed Prince of Liangcheng county; the third son Wei of Prince Fu of Taiyuan was made successor.
translations.idiomatic: Pou predeceased; frail Chuo took Liangcheng while Taiyuan prince Fu's third son Wei inherited the main title.

sentences.zh: 官至侍中、尚書，早薨，子韶立。

translations.literal: He reached palace attendant and minister of writing, died early; son Shao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died young at palace attendant and minister of writing; Shao followed.

sentences.zh: =晃弟太原烈王瓌=

translations.literal: Huang di Taiyuan Lie Wang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, Prince Lie of Taiyuan—Huang's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 太原烈王瓌，字子泉，魏長樂亭侯，改封貴壽鄉侯。

translations.literal: Prince Lie of Taiyuan Gui courtesy Ziquan was Marquis of Changle precinct in Wei and changed to Marquis of Guishou village.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Gui, styled Ziquan, held Changle ting then Guishou township under Wei.

sentences.zh: 曆振威將軍，秘書監，封固始子。

translations.literal: He successively held General Who Displays Might, Palace Library Supervisor, and was enfeoffed Viscount of Gushi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through display-might general and palace librarian to Gushi viscount.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封太原王，邑五千四百九十六戶，就國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Taiyuan with five thousand four hundred ninety-six households and proceeded to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan made him Taiyuan prince at 5,496 households.

sentences.zh: 四年入朝，賜袞冕之服，遷東中郎將。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered court and was granted robe and crown of state; he was promoted General of the Eastern Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Year four brought court robes and eastern gentleman-general rank.

sentences.zh: 十年薨，詔曰：「瑰乃心忠篤，智器雅亮。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died; an edict said, 'Gui's heart was loyal and earnest; intellect and capacity were elegant and bright.
translations.idiomatic: His tenth-year death drew praise for loyalty and bright capacity.

sentences.zh: 歷位文武，有幹事之績。

translations.literal: He successively held civil and military posts and had achievements in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He delivered solid results in civil and martial offices.

sentences.zh: 出臨封土，夷夏懷附，鎮守許都，思謀可紀。

translations.literal: Going out he faced his enfeoffment lands and barbarians and Chinese cherished allegiance; guarding Xu capital his designs merit record.
translations.idiomatic: His province won Yi and Xia allegiance; garrisoning Xu city he strategized memorably.

sentences.zh: 不幸早薨，朕甚悼之。

translations.literal: Unluckily he died young; We greatly mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: His premature death stirred deep imperial mourning.

sentences.zh: 今安厝在近，其追贈前將軍。

translations.literal: Now that burial nears let him be posthumously invested Former General.
translations.idiomatic: With interment at hand the court added posthumous former-general rank.

sentences.zh: 」子顒立，徙封河間王，別有傳。

translations.literal: Son Yong succeeded, transferred enfeoffment to Prince of Hejian; elsewhere there is a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Yong shifted the fief to Hejian—a fuller life appears in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: =瑰弟高陽元王珪=

translations.literal: Younger brother of Prince Lie Gui: Prince Yuan Gui of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan of Gaoyang, Sima Gui—brother of Prince Lie Sima Gui.

sentences.zh: 高陽元王珪，字子璋，少有才望，魏高陽鄉侯。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan of Gaoyang Gui courtesy Zhang had talent and reputation in youth and was Gaoyang village marquis in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Gui, styled Zhang, showed early promise as Gaoyang village marquis.

sentences.zh: 曆河南令，進封湞陽子，拜給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively held magistrate of Henan, advanced to Viscount of Zhenyang, and was appointed Serving Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Henan, rose to Zhenyang viscount, then serving yellow-gate gentleman.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封高陽王，邑五千五百七十戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Gaoyang with five thousand five hundred seventy households.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan invested Gaoyang at 5,570 households.

sentences.zh: 曆北中郎將、督鄴城守諸軍事。

translations.literal: He successively held General of the Northern Gentlemen and supervised Ye city garrison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded northern gentlemen and Ye defenses.

sentences.zh: 入朝，以父孚年高，乞留供養。

translations.literal: Entering court because father Fu was advanced in years he begged to remain and provide support.
translations.idiomatic: Court duty moved him to ask leave to nurse elderly Sima Fu.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書，遷右僕射。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Writing and promoted Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He took the ministry then right vice director.

sentences.zh: 十年薨，詔遣兼大鴻臚持節監護喪事，贈車騎將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died; an edict dispatched concurrent Grand Herald with credentials to supervise funeral affairs and posthumously invested chariot-and-cavalry general with ceremonies equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Year ten brought supervised obsequies and posthumous chariot-and-cavalry honors matching three-dukes rites.

sentences.zh: 珪有美譽於世，而帝甚悼惜之。

translations.literal: Gui had fine reputation in the world yet the emperor deeply mourned and cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrated publicly, he won uncommon imperial grief.

sentences.zh: 無子，詔以太原王輔子緝襲爵。

translations.literal: Having no son an edict ordered Prince Fu of Taiyuan's son Ji to inherit the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Without issue Taiyuan prince Fu's son Ji inherited.

sentences.zh: 緝立五年，薨，諡曰哀。

translations.literal: Ji succeeded five years and died; posthumous title was Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Ji reigned five years with epithet Ai.

sentences.zh: 無子，詔以太原王瑰世子顒子訟為緝後，封真定縣侯。

translations.literal: Having no son an edict ordered Song, son of heir-apparent Yong of Taiyuan Prince Gui, as Ji's successor enfeoffed Marquis of Zhending county.
translations.idiomatic: Still without heirs the throne named Song—grandson in Taiyuan prince Gui's line—as Zhending county marquis to continue Ji.

sentences.zh: =珪弟常山孝王衡=

translations.literal: Gui di Changshan Xiao Wang Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Heng, Prince Xiao of Changshan—Gui's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 常山孝王衡，字子平，魏封德陽鄉侯。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Changshan Heng courtesy Ziping was Deyang village marquis in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Heng, styled Ziping, held Deyang village under Wei.

sentences.zh: 進封汝陽子，為駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He advanced to Viscount of Runyang and became Commandant Steadfast for imperial sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion brought Runyang viscount and commandant for princess consorts.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封常山王，邑三千七百九十戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Changshan with three thousand seven hundred ninety households.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan named him Changshan prince at 3,790 households.

sentences.zh: 二年薨，無子，以安平世子邕第四子敦為嗣。

translations.literal: In the second year he died without sons; Yong heir Yong's fourth son Dun was appointed successor.
translations.idiomatic: Childless after two years Yong's fourth son Dun succeeded.

sentences.zh: =衡弟沛順王景=

translations.literal: Heng di Pei Shun Wang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Prince Shun of Pei—Heng's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 沛順王景，字子文，魏樂安亭侯。

translations.literal: Prince Shun of Pei Jing courtesy Ziwen was Leyang precinct marquis in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jing, styled Ziwen, began as Leyang ting marquis.

sentences.zh: 曆諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He successively held Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand counselor of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封沛王，邑三千四百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Pei with three thousand four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan invested Pei at 3,400 households.

sentences.zh: 立十一年，薨，子韜立。

translations.literal: Eleven years enthroned he died; son Tao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven-year reign ended; Tao inherited.

sentences.zh: 彭城穆王權

translations.literal: Prince Mu of Pengcheng Quan.
