translations.idiomatic: Quan, Prince Mu of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 彭城穆王權，字子輿，宣帝弟魏魯相東武城侯馗之子也。

translations.literal: Prince Mu of Pengcheng Quan courtesy Ziyu was son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Wei Lu governor East Wucheng Marquis Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Quan, styled Ziyu, was son of Sima Kui—Sima Yi's brother and Wei governor of Lu.

sentences.zh: 初襲封，拜冗從僕射。

translations.literal: At first inheriting the enfeoffment he was appointed Supernumerary Master of Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He opened as supernumerary chariot master.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封彭城王，邑二千九百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng with two thousand nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan made him Pengcheng prince at 2,900 households.

sentences.zh: 出為北中郎將、都督鄴城守諸軍事。

translations.literal: He went out as General of the Northern Gentlemen supervising Ye city garrison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Ye's northern gentleman garrison.

sentences.zh: 泰始中入朝，賜袞冕之服。

translations.literal: In Taishi mid-years he entered court and was granted robe and crown of state.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Taishi brought court investiture robes.

sentences.zh: 咸甯元年薨，子元王植立。

translations.literal: In Xianning year one he died; son Prince Yuan Zhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: 275 death; Yuan prince Zhi followed.

sentences.zh: 歷位後將軍，尋拜國子祭酒、太僕卿、侍中、尚書。

translations.literal: He successively held Later General, soon appointed Libationer of the Imperial Academy, Minister of Coachmanship, palace attendant, and minister of writing.
translations.idiomatic: His offices ran rear general, academy libationer, coach minister, palace attendant, and ministry.

sentences.zh: 出為安東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事，代淮南王允鎮壽春，未發。

translations.literal: He was going out as General Who Pacifies the East supervising Yangzhou military affairs replacing Prince Huainan Yun at Shouchun but did not depart.
translations.idiomatic: Named east-pacifier for Yangzhou replacing Yun at Shouchun, he never took up post.

sentences.zh: 或云植助允攻趙王倫，遂以憂薨。

translations.literal: Some say Zhi assisted Yun in attacking Prince Zhao Lun and therefore died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition claims he aided Yun against Sima Lun and died of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎將軍，增封萬五千戶。

translations.literal: He was posthumously invested chariot-and-cavalry general and his enfeoffment was increased by fifteen thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The court added posthumous chariot-and-cavalry honors and boosted his fief by fifteen thousand households.

sentences.zh: 子康王釋立，官至南中郎將、持節、平南將軍，分魯國蕃、薛二縣以益其國，心二萬三千戶。

translations.literal: Son Prince Kang Shi succeeded; he reached Southern Gentlemen General, credential-bearing, Pacifying South General; partitioned Fan and Xue counties of Lu to enlarge his state; total twenty-three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang Sima Shi rose to southern gentleman-general with pacifying-south command, annexed Fan and Xue from Lu, and held twenty-three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 薨，子雄立，坐奔蘇峻伏誅，更以釋子紘嗣。

translations.literal: He died; son Xiong succeeded; Xiong was executed for fleeing to Su Jun; Shi's son Hong was changed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Xiong inherited but died with Su Jun's rebellion; Hong, son of Shi, continued the line.

sentences.zh: =曾孫紘=

translations.literal: Great-grandson Hong.
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandson Hong.

sentences.zh: 紘字偉德，初封堂邑縣公。

translations.literal: Hong courtesy Weide at first was enfeoffed Duke of Tangyi county.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Hong, styled Weide, began as duke of Tangyi county.

sentences.zh: 建興末，元帝承制，以紘繼高密王據。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianxing Yuan Di under emergency regulations ordered Hong to succeed Prince of Gaomi Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianxing Sima Rui assigned Hong to continue Prince Ju of Gaomi's line.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，拜散騎侍郎，遷翊軍校尉、前將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne Hong was appointed irregular cavalry gentleman and promoted Colonel Who Aids the Army and Former General.
translations.idiomatic: After enthronement Hong became supernumerary cavalry attendant, then aide-army colonel and former general.

sentences.zh: 雄之誅也，紘入繼本宗。

translations.literal: When Xiong was executed Hong entered to succeed his root lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's execution brought Hong back into his birth house.

sentences.zh: 拜國子祭酒，加散騎常侍，尋遷大宗正、秘書監。

translations.literal: He was appointed Libationer of the Imperial Academy with additional irregular cavalry attendant; soon promoted Grand Director of the Imperial Clan and Palace Library Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the academy with supernumerary cavalry rank, then headed the imperial clan office and palace library.

sentences.zh: 有風疾，性理不恆。

translations.literal: He had wind illness and his disposition was not constant.
translations.idiomatic: Windstroke unsettled his temperament.

sentences.zh: 或欲上疏陳事，曆示公卿。

translations.literal: Sometimes he wished to submit memorials stating affairs and showed them in turn to dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He would draft memorials and parade them past the high ministers.

sentences.zh: 又杜門讓還章印貂蟬，著《杜門賦》以顯其志。

translations.literal: Again he shut his gate declining to return seals and courtier insignia and composed 'Rhapsody on Shutting the Gate' to display his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed his gates, tried to return insignia, and wrote a rhapsody proclaiming reclusion.

sentences.zh: 由是更拜光祿大夫，領大宗師，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was further appointed Grand Master of Splendid Carriages concurrent Grand Master of the Imperial Clan while irregular attendant remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him splendid-carriages grand master with clan-director duties while keeping cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 後疾甚，馳騁無度，或攻劫軍寺，或扞傷官屬，醜言悖詈，誹謗上下。

translations.literal: Later his illness grew severe; he galloped without restraint, sometimes raiding military offices, sometimes striking officials, ugly words and abusive curses slandering superiors and subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Madness drove him to reckless rides, assaults on yamen, beatings of staff, and foul-mouthed outbursts against everyone.

sentences.zh: 又乘車突入端門，至太極殿前。

translations.literal: He also drove a carriage crashing through the Vermilion Gate to the forecourt of Taiji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rammed a cart through the main palace gate to Taiji's steps.

sentences.zh: 於是御史中丞車灌奏劾，請免紘官，下其國嚴加防錄。

translations.literal: Thereupon Palace Assistant chief Che Guan impeached him requesting Hong be dismissed and his state strictly confined.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Che Guan demanded Hong's removal and house arrest in his domain.

sentences.zh: 成帝詔曰：「王以明德茂親，居宗師之重，宜敷道養德，靜一其操。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng's edict said, 'The prince by bright virtue as a lush kinsman occupies the weight of clan tutor—he ought to spread the Way and nurture virtue and quiet his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdi urged Hong to model restraint as imperial tutor.

sentences.zh: 而頃遊行煩數，冒履風塵。

translations.literal: Yet lately his roaming has been frequent and he braves wind and dust.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept racing about in wind and dust.

sentences.zh: 宜令官屬已下，各以職奉衛，不得令王復有此勞。

translations.literal: Let officials under his household each according to duty attend him and not allow the prince again such labor.
translations.idiomatic: Staff must attend him on duty and spare him these exertions.

sentences.zh: 內外職司，各慎其局。

translations.literal: Inner and outer offices each must be careful of their sphere.
translations.idiomatic: Every bureau must mind its brief.

sentences.zh: 王可解常侍、光祿、宗師，先所給車牛可錄取，賜米布床帳以養疾。

translations.literal: The prince may be relieved of irregular attendant, splendid-carriages, and clan tutor posts; ox carts formerly supplied may be withdrawn; grant rice, cloth, bed, and curtain to nurse illness.
translations.idiomatic: Strip his concurrent titles and carts but supply grain and bedding for convalescence.

sentences.zh: 」薨，贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously gifted irregular cavalry attendant and golden-purple splendid-carriages grand master.
translations.idiomatic: Death brought posthumous supernumerary cavalry attendant and golden-purple grand master honors.

sentences.zh: 二子：玄、俊。

translations.literal: Two sons: Xuan and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He left sons Xuan and Jun.

sentences.zh: 玄嗣立。

translations.literal: Xuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan inherited.

sentences.zh: 會庚戌制不得藏戶，玄匿五戶，桓溫表玄犯禁，收付廷尉。

translations.literal: When the gengxu household-registration reform forbade concealing households Xuan hid five households; Huan Wen memorialized the offense and had him seized for the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Household reform caught Xuan hiding five families; Huan Wen sent him to justice.

sentences.zh: 既而宥之，位至中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was soon pardoned and reached Palace Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He won amnesty and rose to secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 薨，子弘之立，位至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died; son Hong zhi succeeded and reached irregular cavalry attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Hong zhi inherited and became supernumerary cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 薨，子邵之立。

translations.literal: He died; son Shao zhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shao zhi followed.

sentences.zh: 薨，子崇之立。

translations.literal: He died; son Chong zhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Chong zhi followed.

sentences.zh: 薨，子緝之立。

translations.literal: He died; son Ji zhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ji zhi followed.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song accepted the abdication the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu Song takeover ended the principality.

sentences.zh: 紘子俊

translations.literal: Hong's son Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Jun.

sentences.zh: 恭王俊字道度，出嗣高密王略，官至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Prince Gong Jun courtesy Daodu went out to succeed Prince of Gaomi Lue and reached irregular cavalry attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong Sima Jun, styled Daodu, continued Lue of Gaomi and rose to supernumerary cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 薨，子敬王純之立，曆臨川內史、司農少府卿、太宰右長史。

translations.literal: He died; son Prince Jing Chun zhi succeeded and successively held interior governor of Linchuan, junior minister of agriculture, senior steward left chief clerk of grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Chun zhi governed Linchuan and served agriculture and tutor bureaus.

sentences.zh: 薨，子恢之立。

translations.literal: He died; son Hui zhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Hui zhi inherited.

sentences.zh: 義熙末，以給事中兼太尉，修謁洛陽園陵。

translations.literal: At the end of Yixi he as consultant concurrently grand commandant repaired and visited Luoyang mausolea.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yixi he doubled as grand commandant tending western tombs.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song accepted the abdication the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song shuttered the fief.

sentences.zh: =高密文獻王泰=

translations.literal: Prince Wenxian of Gaomi Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tai, Prince Wenxian of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 高密文獻王泰，字子舒，彭城穆王權之弟，魏陽亭侯，補陽翟令，遷扶風太守。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxian of Gaomi Tai courtesy Zishu was younger brother of Prince Mu of Pengcheng Quan, Marquis of Yang precinct in Wei; supplied Yangdi magistrate; promoted governor of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tai, styled Zishu, was Sima Quan's brother—Yang ting marquis, Yangdi magistrate, Fufeng governor.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封隴西王，邑三千二百戶，拜遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Longxi with three thousand two hundred households and appointed roving-strike general.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan made him Longxi prince at 3,200 households with roving-strike command.

sentences.zh: 出為兗州刺史，加鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Yan Province with additional general Who Displays Hawk banner.
translations.idiomatic: He shepherded Yan with hawk-banner general rank.

sentences.zh: 遷使持節、都督甯益二州諸軍事、安西將軍，領益州刺史，稱疾不行。

translations.literal: He was promoted credential-bearing supervisor of Ning and Yi military affairs and Pacifying West General concurrent Yi Inspector but pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Ning-Yi pacifying-west orders went unfulfilled on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 轉安北將軍，代兄權督鄴城守事。

translations.literal: He transferred to Pacifying North General replacing elder brother Quan supervising Ye garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded brother Quan as pacifying-north chief at Ye.

sentences.zh: 安西將軍、都督關中事。

translations.literal: Pacifying West General supervising Guanzhong affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also held pacifying-west charge over Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 太康初，入為散騎常侍、前將軍，領鄴城門校尉，以疾去官。

translations.literal: Early Taikang he entered as irregular cavalry attendant and former general concurrent colonel of Ye gates but resigned for illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early Taikang brought palace posts and Ye gate command until illness retired him.

sentences.zh: 後代下邳王晃為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Later he replaced Prince of Xiapi Huang as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He later succeeded Sima Huang as left vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮西將軍，領護西戎校尉、假節，代扶風王駿都督關中軍事，以疾還京師。

translations.literal: He went out as Guarding West General concurrent colonel of western tribes with credentials replacing Prince of Fufeng Jun supervising Guanzhong military affairs but returned to capital for illness.
translations.idiomatic: Western command and tribal colonelcy ended when sickness recalled him.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，代石鑒為司空，尋領太子太保。

translations.literal: Early Yongxi he replaced Shi Jian as Minister of Works and soon concurrent junior tutor to heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi opened with minister of works and heir-apparent junior tutor posts.

sentences.zh: 及楊駿誅，泰領駿營，加侍中，給步兵二千五百人，騎五百匹。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun was executed Tai took over Jun's camp with additional palace attendant, two thousand five hundred infantry, and five hundred cavalry granted.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's purge handed Tai the camp plus two thousand five hundred foot and five hundred horse.

sentences.zh: 泰固辭，乃給千兵百騎。

translations.literal: Tai firmly declined so only one thousand troops and one hundred cavalry were given.
translations.idiomatic: He bargained the guard down to one thousand foot and one hundred horse.

sentences.zh: 楚王瑋之被收，泰嚴兵將救之，祭酒丁綏諫曰：「公為宰相，不可輕動。

translations.literal: When Prince of Chu Wei was seized Tai drew up troops intending to rescue him; Libationer Ding Sui remonstrated saying, 'You are chief minister—you cannot move rashly.'
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tai mobilized to free Sima Wei until Ding Sui warned a premier must not stir recklessly.

sentences.zh: 且夜中倉卒，宜遣人參審定問。

translations.literal: Moreover midnight crisis requires sending men to investigate clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Send scouts first in a midnight crisis.

sentences.zh: 」泰從之。

translations.literal: Tai followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Tai agreed.

sentences.zh: 瑋既誅，乃以泰錄尚書事，遷太尉，守尚書令，改封高密王，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: After Wei was executed Tai was put in charge of Ministry records, promoted Grand Commandant while holding Minister Director, changed enfeoffment to Prince of Gaomi with ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's fall made Tai acting minister chief, then grand commandant with Gaomi at ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 薨，追贈太傅。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously invested Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous grand mentor followed his death.

sentences.zh: 泰性廉靜，不近聲色。

translations.literal: Tai's nature was honest and quiet; he did not draw near music and women.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste and retiring, he shunned entertainment and concubines.

sentences.zh: 雖為宰輔，食大國之租，服飾肴膳如布衣寒士。

translations.literal: Though he was chief minister eating great-state rents his dress and food were like a poor commoner scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Despite ministerial income he dressed and ate like a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 任真簡率，每朝會，不識者不知其王公也。

translations.literal: Straightforward and plain at court assemblies strangers did not know he was a prince duke.
translations.idiomatic: At audience strangers mistook him for a common official.

sentences.zh: 事視恭謹，居喪哀戚，謙虛下物，為宗室儀錶。

translations.literal: Serving kin he was respectful and cautious; in mourning grief-stricken; humble toward others—he was model for the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Filial in mourning and deferential, he set clan standard.

sentences.zh: 當時諸王，惟泰及下邳王晃以節制見稱。

translations.literal: Among princes of the time only Tai and Prince of Xiapi Huang were praised for restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Only Tai and Sima Huang won esteem for self-control.

sentences.zh: 雖並不能振施，其餘莫得比焉。

translations.literal: Though neither could relieve distress broadly none others matched them.
translations.idiomatic: Neither dispensed charity widely yet none surpassed their discipline.

sentences.zh: 泰四子：越、騰、略、模。

translations.literal: Tai had four sons: Yue, Teng, Lue, Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons: Yue, Teng, Lue, Mo.

sentences.zh: 越自有傳。

translations.literal: Yue has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yue appears elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 騰出後叔父，弟略立。

translations.literal: Teng went out to succeed uncle; younger brother Lue succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Teng was adopted out; Lue inherited.

sentences.zh: 子孝王略

translations.literal: Son Prince Xiao Lue.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Sima Lue.

sentences.zh: 孝王略，字元簡，孝敬慈順，小心下士，少有父風。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao Lue courtesy Yuanjian was respectful, mild, and obedient, humble toward scholars, having somewhat his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lue, styled Yuanjian, echoed his father's modest courtesy.

sentences.zh: 元康初，湣懷太子在東宮，選大臣子弟有名稱者以為賓友，略與華恆等並侍左右。

translations.literal: Early Yuankang Crown Prince Minhuai was in the eastern palace and chose sons of eminent ministers with reputation as guests and friends; Lue together with Hua Heng and others attended left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang saw Lue among Minhuai's cultivated companions with Hua Heng.

sentences.zh: 曆散騎黃門侍郎、散騎常侍、秘書監，出為安南將軍、持節、都督沔南諸軍事，遷安北將軍、都督青州諸軍事。

translations.literal: He successively held irregular cavalry yellow-gate gentleman, irregular cavalry attendant, palace library supervisor; went out Pacifying South General credential-bearing supervising Hannan military affairs; promoted Pacifying North General supervising Qing province military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His career ran palace posts then southern then northern frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 略逼青州刺史程牧，牧避之，略自領州。

translations.literal: Lue pressured Qing Inspector Cheng Mu until Mu yielded and Lue personally headed the province.
translations.idiomatic: He bullied Cheng Mu aside and seized Qingzhou himself.

sentences.zh: 永興初，㡉令劉根起兵東萊，誑惑百姓，眾以萬數，攻略於臨淄，略不能距，走保聊城。

translations.literal: Early Yongxing Magistrate Liu Gen of Yi county raised troops in Donglai deluding commoners tens of thousands strong raiding Lue at Linzi; Lue could not resist and fled defending Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing opened with Liu Gen's Donglai rising that drove Lue from Linzi to Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，遷使持節、都督荊州諸軍事、征南大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended Lue was promoted credential-bearing supervisor of Jing military affairs, southern expedition grand marshal with independent headquarters matching Three Lords.
translations.idiomatic: Huai made him credential-bearing Jing commander with three-dukes parity staff.

sentences.zh: 京兆流人王逌與叟人郝洛聚眾數千，屯于冠軍。

translations.literal: Metropolitan wanderers Wang Di and elder tribesman Hao Luo gathered several thousand men camping at Guanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees Wang Di and Hao Luo mustered thousands at Guanjun.

sentences.zh: 略遣參軍崔曠率將軍皮初、張洛等討逌，為逌所譎，戰敗。

translations.literal: Lue sent aide Cui Kuang leading generals Pi Chu and Zhang Luo to punish Di; Di tricked them and they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kuang's column fell to Wang Di's stratagem.

sentences.zh: 略更遣左司馬曹攄統曠等進逼逌。

translations.literal: Lue again sent Left Major Cao Shu commanding Kuang and others pressing Di.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shu drove Kuang forward again.

sentences.zh: 將大戰，曠在後密自退走，攄軍無繼，戰敗，死之。

translations.literal: About to fight a great battle Kuang secretly withdrew to the rear; Shu's army lacked support, was defeated, and Shu died.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang fled mid-battle; unsupported Shu died fighting.

sentences.zh: 略乃赦曠罪，復遣部將韓松又督曠攻逌，逌降。

translations.literal: Lue then pardoned Kuang's crime and again dispatched subordinate Han Song supervising Kuang attacking Di; Di surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hong pardoned Kuang; Han Song helped force Wang Di's capitulation.

sentences.zh: 尋進開府，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced independent headquarters with additional irregular cavalry attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He soon gained full staff plus supernumerary cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 薨，追贈侍中、太尉，子據立。

translations.literal: He died posthumously gifted palace attendant and grand commandant; son Ju succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous attendant and grand commandant honors preceded Ju's succession.

sentences.zh: 薨，無子，以彭城康王子紘為嗣。

translations.literal: He died without sons; Prince Kang of Pengcheng's son Hong was appointed successor.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he passed to Hong from Pengcheng's Kang line.

sentences.zh: 其後紘歸本宗，立紘子俊以奉其祀。

translations.literal: Later Hong returned to root lineage; Hong's son Jun was established to maintain his sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Hong reverted to his birth house; Jun kept Lue's line alive.

sentences.zh: 略兄新蔡武哀王騰

translations.literal: Lue's elder brother Prince Wuai of Xincai Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Lue's elder brother Sima Teng, Prince Wuai of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 新蔡武哀王騰，字元邁，少拜冗從僕射，封東嬴公，曆南陽、魏郡太守，所在稱職，徵為宗正，遷太常，轉持節、寧北將軍、都督并州諸軍事、并州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince Wuai of Xincai Teng courtesy Yuanmai in youth was appointed supernumerary chariot master and enfeoffed Duke of Dongying; successively governor of Nanyang and Wei commandery where he was praised competent; summoned Grand Director of the Imperial Clan; promoted Minister of Ceremonies; transferred credential-bearing Pacifying North General supervising Bing military affairs and Bing Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng rose from Dongying duke through capable governorships to Bing commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 惠帝討成都王穎，六軍敗績。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned against Prince of Chengdu Ying the six armies were routed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's expedition against Sima Ying collapsed.

sentences.zh: 騰與安北將軍王浚共殺穎所署幽州刺史和演，率眾討穎。

translations.literal: Teng together with Pacifying North General Wang Jun jointly killed Inspector of You appointed by Ying—He Yan—and led hosts against Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Teng joined Wang Jun executing He Yan then marched on Ying.

sentences.zh: 穎遣北中郎將王斌距戰，浚率鮮卑騎擊斌，騰為後系，大破之。

translations.literal: Ying dispatched Northern Gentlemen General Wang Bin to resist; Jun led Xianbei horse striking Bin while Teng covered the rear routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei cavalry under Wang Jun shattered Wang Bin while Teng held the rear.

sentences.zh: 穎懼，挾帝歸洛陽，進騰位安北將軍。

translations.literal: Ying feared and escorted the emperor back to Luoyang; Teng was advanced Pacifying North General.
translations.idiomatic: Ying fled west with Huiyi while Teng gained pacifying-north promotion.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，遷車騎將軍，都督鄴城守諸軍事，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: Early Yongjia he was promoted chariot-and-cavalry general supervising Ye garrison stationed at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia named him chariot-and-cavalry chief at Ye.

sentences.zh: 又以迎駕之勳，改封新蔡王。

translations.literal: Again for merit welcoming the imperial carriage his enfeoffment was changed Prince of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the throne earned the Xincai princedom.

sentences.zh: 初，騰發并州，次於真定。

translations.literal: At first when Teng set out from Bing Province he halted at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Bing he paused at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 值大雪，平地數尺，營門前方數丈雪融不積，騰怪而掘之，得玉馬，高尺許，表獻之。

translations.literal: It happened there was great snow several chi deep on level ground; before the camp gate several zhang of ground showed melted snow not accumulating; Teng wondered and dug obtaining a jade horse about a chi high which he memorialized and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Snow melted oddly at his gate; digging revealed a jade horse sent to court.

sentences.zh: 其後公師籓與平陽人汲桑等為群盜，起於清河鄃縣，眾千餘人，寇頓丘，以葬成都王穎為辭，載穎主而行，與張泓故將李豐等將攻鄴。

translations.literal: Later duke-lord Shi Fan with Pingyang men Ji Sang and others formed bandit gangs rising in Shu county of Qinghe over one thousand strong raiding Dunqiu using burying Prince of Chengdu Ying as pretext loading Ying's spirit tablet marching with Zhang Hong's old general Li Feng intending to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang's gang marched under Ying's tablet to threaten Ye.

sentences.zh: 騰曰：「孤在并州七年，胡圍城不能克。

translations.literal: Teng said, 'I was at Bing seven years and barbarians besieging the city could not overcome it.'
translations.idiomatic: Teng boasted seven Bing years had broken barbarian sieges.

sentences.zh: 汲桑小賊，何足憂也。

translations.literal: Ji Sang petty bandits—what worth worry.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang was too trivial to fear.

sentences.zh: 」及豐等至，騰不能守，率輕騎而走，為豐所害。

translations.literal: When Feng and others arrived Teng could not defend and led light horse fleeing and was killed by Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The raid overwhelmed him; fleeing lightly armed he fell to Feng.

sentences.zh: 四子：虞、矯、紹、確。

translations.literal: Four sons: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons survived: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que.

sentences.zh: 虞有勇力，騰之被害，虞逐豐，豐投水而死。

translations.literal: Yu had courage and strength; when Teng was harmed Yu pursued Feng who threw himself in water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu avenged his father driving Feng into the river.

sentences.zh: 是日，虞及矯、紹並钜鹿太守崔曼、車騎長史羊恆、從事中郎蔡克等又為豐餘黨所害，及諸名家流移依鄴者，死亡並盡。

translations.literal: That same day Yu together with Jiao and Shao and Julu governor Cui Man chariot-and-cavalry chief clerk Yang Heng consultant Cai Ke were again harmed by Feng's remaining faction and renowned families taking refuge at Ye perished altogether.
translations.idiomatic: The bloodbath wiped Julu officials and refugee clans at Ye.

sentences.zh: 初，鄴中雖府庫虛竭，而騰資用甚饒。

translations.literal: At first though Ye granaries were exhausted Teng's private wealth was very ample.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's arsenals stood empty yet Teng hoarded wealth.

sentences.zh: 性儉嗇，無所振惠，臨急，乃賜將士米可數升，帛各丈尺，是以人不為用，遂致於禍。

translations.literal: By nature stingy he showed no generosity; facing crisis he then gifted officers several sheng of rice and bolts only one zhang therefore men would not serve him and ruin followed.
translations.idiomatic: His miserly handfuls of grain and cloth bought no loyalty and brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 及苟晞救鄴，桑還平陽。

translations.literal: When Gou Xi relieved Ye Sang returned to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi's relief sent Ji Sang back toward Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 于時盛夏，屍爛壞不可復識，騰及三子骸骨不獲。

translations.literal: It was then deep summer; corpses rotted beyond recognition and Teng's and his three sons' bones could not be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Midsummer heat left bodies unidentifiable; Sima Teng and his three sons never received decent burial.

sentences.zh: 庶子確立。

translations.literal: The cadet son Que succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Younger-son Sima Que inherited.

sentences.zh: 莊王確，字嗣安，曆東中郎將、都督豫州諸軍事，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang Que courtesy Sian successively held Eastern Gentlemen General supervising Yu military affairs stationed at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Que, styled Sian, commanded Yu from Xuchang as eastern gentleman-general.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，為石勒所害。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia he was harmed by Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le killed him at Yongjia's close.

sentences.zh: 無子，初以章武王混子滔奉其祀，其後復以汝南威王祐子弼為確後。

translations.literal: Having no sons at first Prince Hun's son Tao of Zhangwu was appointed to maintain his sacrifices; afterward Prince You's son Bi of Runan mightily was made Que's successor.
translations.idiomatic: First Tao continued his line; later Bi of Runan replaced him.

sentences.zh: 薨，無子，又以弼弟邈嗣確，位至侍中。

translations.literal: He died without sons; again Bi's younger brother Miao succeeded Que reaching palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Miao followed Bi without issue of his own.

sentences.zh: 薨，子晃立，拜散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He died; son Huang succeeded appointed irregular cavalry gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Huang inherited as supernumerary cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 桓溫廢武陵王，免晃為庶人，徙衡陽。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen deposed Prince of Wuling Huang was degraded commoner and banished Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's coup reduced Huang to commoner exile in Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝立晃弟崇繼邈後，為奴所害，子惠立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu enthroned Huang's younger brother Chong continued Miao's line and was harmed by slaves; son Hui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Chong continued Miao yet fell to household slaves; Hui followed.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song accepted the abdication the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song ended the fief.

sentences.zh: 略弟南陽王模

translations.literal: Younger brother of Lue Mo Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang—Lue's brother.

sentences.zh: 南陽王模，字元表，少好學，與元帝及范陽王虓俱有稱於宗室。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanyang Mo courtesy Yuanbiao in youth loved learning and together with Yuan Di and Prince Xiao of Fanyang was praised within the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Mo, styled Yuanbiao, studied hard alongside Sima Rui and Sima Xiao.

sentences.zh: 初封平昌公。

translations.literal: At first enfeoffed Duke of Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Pingchang duke.

sentences.zh: 惠帝末，拜冗從僕射，累遷太子庶子、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Late Emperor Hui he was appointed supernumerary chariot master and progressively promoted heir-apparent household aide and supernumerary irregular cavalry attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Late Hui's reign brought chariot master through heir staff to supernumerary cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎奔長安，東海王越以模為北中郎將，鎮鄴。

translations.literal: When Prince of Chengdu Ying fled to Chang'an Prince of Donghai Yue appointed Mo Northern Gentlemen General guarding Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's flight west left Mo northern gentleman at Ye under Yue.

sentences.zh: 永興初，成都王穎故帳下督公師籓、樓權、郝昌等攻鄴，模左右謀應之。

translations.literal: Early Yongxing Chengdu Prince Ying's former overseer Gongshi Fan Lou Quan Hao Chang and others attacked Ye; Mo's attendants plotted to respond within.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing opened with Gongshi Fan's siege and traitors inside Ye.

sentences.zh: 廣平太守丁邵率眾救模，范陽王虓又遣兗州刺史苟晞援之，籓等散走。

translations.literal: Guangping governor Ding Shao led hosts relieving Mo; Prince Xiao of Fanyang again dispatched Yan Inspector Gou Xi aiding them; Fan and others scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shao and Gou Xi lifted the siege and routed Fan.

sentences.zh: 遷鎮東大將軍，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: Mo was promoted Guarding East Grand Marshal stationed Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He became guarding-east marshal at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 進爵南陽王。

translations.literal: He advanced noble rank Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，轉征西大將軍、開府、都督秦雍梁益諸軍事，代河間王顒鎮關中。

translations.literal: Early Yongjia he transferred western expedition grand marshal independent headquarters supervising Qin Yong Liang Yi military affairs replacing Prince of Hejian Yong guarding Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia gave him four-province western command replacing Sima Yong.

sentences.zh: 模感丁邵之德，敕國人為邵生立碑。

translations.literal: Mo grateful for Ding Shao's virtue ordered his people erect a living monument to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized Ding Shao with a standing stone.

sentences.zh: 時關中饑荒，百姓相噉，加以疾癘，盜賊公行。

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong starved; commoners devoured one another; pestilence added; bandits operated openly.
translations.idiomatic: Famine cannibalism plague and brigandage ravaged Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 模力不能制，乃鑄銅人鐘鼎為釜器以易穀，議者非之。

translations.literal: Mo's strength could not control it so he cast bronze men bells and tripods into cauldrons to trade for grain; critics condemned this.
translations.idiomatic: He melted ritual bronzes for grain swaps—widely condemned.

sentences.zh: 東海王越表徵模為司空，遣中書監傅祗代之。

translations.literal: Prince of Donghai Yue memorialized summoning Mo as Minister of Works sending Palace Library Director Fu Zhi to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue summoned Mo to minister of works under Fu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 模謀臣淳於定說模曰：「關中天府之國，霸王之地。

translations.literal: Mo's strategist Chunyu Ding advised Mo saying 'Guanzhong is heaven's storehouse—the ground of hegemons.'
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Ding called Guanzhong the natural seat of empire.

sentences.zh: 今以不能綏撫而還，既於聲望有虧，又公兄弟唱起大事，而並在朝廷，若自強則有專權之罪，弱則受制於人，非公之利也。

translations.literal: Now unable to soothe and returning damages your renown; moreover your lordship's brothers launched great affairs yet both remain at court—if you strengthen yourself you incur monopolizing guilt; if weak you fall under others' control—not to your advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving loses prestige; staying weak among powerful brothers courts ruin.

sentences.zh: 」模納其言，不就徵。

translations.literal: Mo accepted his words and did not obey the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Mo stayed put ignoring the recall.

sentences.zh: 表遣世子保為西中郎將、東羌校尉，鎮上邽，秦州刺史裴苞距之。

translations.literal: He memorialized dispatching heir-apparent Bao as Western Gentlemen General Eastern Qiang colonel guarding Shanggui; Qin Inspector Pei Bao resisted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent heir Bao to Shanggui against Pei Bao's block.

sentences.zh: 模使帳下都尉陳安率眾攻苞，苞奔安定。

translations.literal: Mo ordered household Commandant Chen An leading hosts attacking Bao; Bao fled Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An drove Pei Bao to Anding.

sentences.zh: 太守賈疋以郡迎苞，模遣軍司謝班伐疋，疋退盧水。

translations.literal: Governor Jia Ya of the commandery welcomed Bao with the district; Mo dispatched army director Xie Ban attacking Ya; Ya withdrew to Lushui.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Ya's welcome drew Xie Ban until Ya fled to Lushui.

sentences.zh: 其年，進位太尉、大都督。

translations.literal: That year he advanced Grand Commandant grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: Same year brought grand commandant and supreme command.

sentences.zh: 洛京傾覆，模使牙門趙染戍蒲阪，染求馮翊太守不得，怒，率眾降于劉聰。

translations.literal: When Luoyang collapsed Mo sent gate officer Zhao Ran guarding Puban; Ran sought Fufeng governor unsuccessfully angrily led hosts surrendering to Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's fall and Zhao Ran's pique handed Liu Cong an opening.

sentences.zh: 聰使其子粲及染攻長安，模使淳於定距之，為染所敗。

translations.literal: Cong ordered son Can and Ran attacking Chang'an; Mo sent Chunyu Ding resisting; defeated by Ran.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can and Zhao Ran routed Ding before Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 士眾離叛，倉庫虛竭，軍祭酒韋輔曰：「事急矣，早降可以免。

translations.literal: Troops deserted; granaries emptied; army libationer Wei Fu said 'Matters are desperate—early surrender can spare you.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fu urged immediate capitulation.

sentences.zh: 」模從之，遂降於染。

translations.literal: Mo followed this and thereupon surrendered to Ran.
translations.idiomatic: Mo yielded to Zhao Ran.

sentences.zh: 染箕踞攘袂數模之罪，送詣粲。

translations.literal: Ran squatted spreading sleeves counting Mo's crimes and sent him to Can.
translations.idiomatic: Ran humiliated Mo then handed him to Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 粲殺之，以模妃劉氏賜胡張本為妻。

translations.literal: Can killed him and gave Mo's consort Lady Liu to Hu Zhang Ben as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Can executed Mo and gifted his wife to Zhang Ben.

sentences.zh: 子保立。

translations.literal: Son Bao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Bao inherited.

sentences.zh: 保字景度，少有文義，好述作。

translations.literal: Bao courtesy Jingdu in youth had literary skill loving composition.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Bao, styled Jingdu, loved letters young.

sentences.zh: 初拜南陽國世子。

translations.literal: At first appointed heir of Nanyang state.
translations.idiomatic: First named heir of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 模遇害，保在邽上。

translations.literal: When Mo met harm Bao was at Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's death found Bao still on Qi heights.

sentences.zh: 其後賈疋死，裴苞又為張軌所殺，保全有秦州之地，自號大司馬，承制置百官。

translations.literal: Later after Jia Ya died and Pei Bao was again killed by Zhang Gui Bao wholly held Qin Province styling himself Grand Marshal under emergency regulations establishing hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: After Ya and Pei Bao fell Bao seized Qin as self-declared grand marshal with full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 隴右氐羌並從之，涼州刺史張寔遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: Di and Qiang of Longyou alike followed him; Liang Inspector Zhang Shi sent envoys tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou tribes rallied; Zhang Shi offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 及湣帝即位，以保為右丞相，加侍中、都督陝西諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended Bao was named right chancellor with additional palace attendant supervising Shanxi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Min appointed him right chancellor over Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋進位相國。

translations.literal: Soon advanced ceremonial prime minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon ceremonial prime minister followed.

sentences.zh: 模之敗也，都尉陳安歸於保，保命統精勇千餘人以討羌，寵遇甚厚。

translations.literal: When Mo was defeated Commandant Chen An joined Bao; Bao ordered him command picked warriors over one thousand against Qiang lavishing favor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An joined Bao and led picked troops against Qiang with royal favor.

sentences.zh: 保將張春等疾之，譖安有異志，請除之，保不許。

translations.literal: Bao's generals Zhang Chun and others envied him slandering An harboring rebellion requesting execution; Bao forbade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun plotted against Chen An; Bao refused.

sentences.zh: 春等輒伏客以刺安，安被創，馳還隴城，遣使詣保，貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: Chun and others then hid guests stabbing An; An wounded galloped back to Longcheng dispatching envoys to Bao tribute unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Assassins wounded An who kept sending tribute from Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 湣帝之蒙塵也，保自稱晉王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min suffered exile Bao styled himself King of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Min's flight led Bao to claim Jin kingship.

sentences.zh: 時上邽大饑，士眾窘困，張春奉保之南安。

translations.literal: Then Shanggui greatly starved troops distressed Zhang Chun conducted Bao to Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Famine drove Zhang Chun to evacuate Bao toward Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 陳安自號秦州刺史，稱籓于劉曜。

translations.literal: Chen An styled himself Qin Inspector declaring vassalage to Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An took Qin title while serving Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 春復奉保奔桑城，將投于張寔。

translations.literal: Chun again conducted Bao fleeing Sang castle intending to join Zhang Shi.
translations.idiomatic: They aimed for Zhang Shi via Sang.

sentences.zh: 寔使兵迎保，實禦之也。

translations.literal: Shi sent troops welcoming Bao truly to block him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi's escort meant to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，保病薨，時年二十七。

translations.literal: That year Bao died ill age twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died ill at twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 保體質豐偉，嘗自稱重八百斤。

translations.literal: Bao's body was stout; he once claimed weight eight hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: He boasted eight hundred jin bulk.

sentences.zh: 喜睡，痿疾，不能禦婦人。

translations.literal: He loved sleep suffered wasting illness could not bed women.
translations.idiomatic: Somnolence and impotence plagued him.

sentences.zh: 無子，張春立宗室司馬瞻奉保後。

translations.literal: Having no son Zhang Chun established clansman Sima Zhan to continue Bao's offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, Zhan continued his house under Zhang Chun.

sentences.zh: 陳安舉兵攻春，春走，瞻降于安，安送詣劉曜，曜殺之。

translations.literal: Chen An raised troops attacking Chun; Chun fled Zhan surrendered to An who delivered him to Liu Yao who executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An crushed Zhang Chun and sent Zhan to his death at Liu Yao's court.

sentences.zh: 安迎保喪，以天子禮葬于上邽，諡曰元。

translations.literal: An welcomed Bao's coffin burying him at Shanggui by Son of Heaven rites posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An buried Bao as emperor with Yuan epithet.

sentences.zh: =范陽康王綏=

translations.literal: Prince Kang of Fanyang Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Sui, Prince Kang of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 范陽康王綏，字子都，彭城王權季弟也，初為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Prince Kang of Fanyang Sui courtesy Zidu was youngest brother of Prince Mu of Pengcheng Quan beginning as grand counselor of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Sui, styled Zidu, was Quan's youngest brother—grand counselor first.

sentences.zh: 受封，在位十五年。

translations.literal: Receiving enfeoffment he remained fifteen years on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned fifteen years.

sentences.zh: 薨，子虓立焉。

translations.literal: He died; son Xiao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 子虓

translations.literal: Son Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xiao.

sentences.zh: 虓字武會，少好學，馳譽，研考經記，清辯，能言論。

translations.literal: Xiao courtesy Wuhui in youth loved learning riding fame researching classics lucid in debate skilled speech.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiao, styled Wuhui, was a famed scholar-orator.

sentences.zh: 以宗室選拜散騎常侍，累遷尚書。

translations.literal: Chosen from imperial clan appointed irregular cavalry attendant progressively promoted minister of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Clan selection brought cavalry attendant then ministry posts.

sentences.zh: 出為安南將軍、都督豫州諸軍事、持節，鎮許昌，進位征南將軍。

translations.literal: He went out Pacifying South General supervising Yu military affairs credential-bearing stationed Xuchang promoted southern expedition general.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Yu from Xuchang southward through pacifying and expedition ranks.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒表立成都王穎為太弟，為王浚所破，挾天子還洛陽。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Yong memorialized establishing Chengdu Prince Ying heir-apparent; defeated by Wang Jun he escorted Son of Heaven back Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's heir plot collapsed under Wang Jun forcing return east.

sentences.zh: 虓與東平王楙、鎮東將軍周馥等上言曰：

translations.literal: Xiao together with Prince of Dongping Mao Guarding East General Zhou Fu and others submitted memorial saying
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiao Mao and Zhou Fu jointly petitioned:

sentences.zh: 又表曰：「成都王失道，為奸邪所誤，論王之身，不宜深責。

translations.literal: Again memorializing 'Chengdu Prince lost the Way misled by wicked favorites judging the prince's person ought not be deeply blamed.
translations.idiomatic: They argued Ying deserved mercy not harsh deposition.

sentences.zh: 且先帝遺體，陛下群弟，自元康以來，罪戮相等，實海內所為匈匈，而臣等所以痛心。

translations.literal: Moreover former emperor's bodily heirs Your Majesty's junior brothers since Yuankang executions match in toll truly why realm churns and why we ache.
translations.idiomatic: Royal brothers' slaughter since Yuankang unsettled the empire.

sentences.zh: 今廢成都，更封一邑，宜其必許。

translations.literal: Now deposing Chengdu changing enfeoffment one canton he ought surely consent.
translations.idiomatic: Offer Ying a lesser fief instead.

sentences.zh: 若廢黜尋有禍害，既傷陛下矜慈之恩，又令遠近恆謂公族無復骨肉之情，此實臣等內省悲慚，無顏于四海也。

translations.literal: If deposition soon brings calamity it wounds Your Majesty's compassionate grace and lets far and near forever say the ducal kin lack flesh-and-blood feeling—truly our inward shame without face before the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Harshness would shame the throne and clan.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下察臣忠款。

translations.literal: Beg Your Majesty perceive our loyal sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: They pled sincerity.

sentences.zh: 」於是虓先率眾自許屯于滎陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiao first led hosts from Xu camping at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao marched to Xingyang first.

sentences.zh: 會惠帝西遷，虓與從兄平昌公模、長史馮嵩等刑白馬喢血而盟，推東海王越為盟主，虓都督河北諸軍事、驃騎將軍、持節，領豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui moved west Xiao together with cousin Pingchang duke Mo chief clerk Feng Song slaughtered white horse smearing blood in covenant elevating Prince of Donghai Yue covenant lord; Xiao supervised Hebei military affairs champion general credential-bearing concurrent Yu Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Western flight triggered blood pact naming Yue leader with Xiao commanding Hebei and Yu.

sentences.zh: 劉喬不受越等節度，乘虛破許。

translations.literal: Liu Qiao refused obeying Yue and others exploiting emptiness broke Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao seized Xu defying Yue.

sentences.zh: 虓自拔渡河，王浚表虓領翼州刺史，資以兵馬。

translations.literal: Xiao extricated himself crossing the river; Wang Jun memorialized Xiao commanding Ji Inspector supplying troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun backed Xiao as Ji commander with materiel.

sentences.zh: 虓入翼州發兵，又南濟河，破喬等。

translations.literal: Xiao entered Ji Province raising troops again crossing south the river defeating Qiao and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao rallied Ji forces and crushed Liu Qiao south of the river.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒聞喬敗，斬張方，傳首於越。

translations.literal: Prince Yong hearing Qiao defeated executed Zhang Fang sending head to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yong killed Zhang Fang after Qiao's defeat.

sentences.zh: 越與虓西迎帝，而顒出奔。

translations.literal: Yue together with Xiao west welcoming emperor while Yong fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and Xiao retrieved Huiyi while Yong ran.

sentences.zh: 於是奉天子還都，拜虓為司徒。

translations.literal: Thereupon elevating Son of Heaven restoring capital Xiao was appointed Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: They restored Luoyang naming Xiao minister of education.

sentences.zh: 暴疾薨，時年三十七。

translations.literal: Sudden illness died age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 無子，養模子黎為嗣，黎隨模就國，于長安遇害。

translations.literal: Having no sons he adopted Mo's son Li successor; Li followed Mo to state harmed at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Childless Li continued Mo's line and died at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 濟南惠王遂

translations.literal: Prince Hui of Jinan Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Sui, Prince Hui of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 濟南惠王遂，字子伯，宣帝弟魏鴻臚丞恂之子也。

translations.literal: Prince Hui of Jinan Sui courtesy Zibo was son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Wei Grand Herald Assistant Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Sui, styled Zibo, was Sima Xun's son—Sima Yi's nephew.

sentences.zh: 仕魏關內侯，進封平昌亭侯，曆典軍郎將。

translations.literal: Serving Wei district marquis within passes advanced Marquis of Pingchang precinct successively holding army corps captain.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he rose from secondary marquis to Pingchang ting through army posts.

sentences.zh: ，轉封武城鄉侯、督鄴城守諸軍事、北中郎將。

translations.literal: Transferred enfeoffment Wucheng village marquis supervising Ye garrison Northern Gentlemen General.
translations.idiomatic: Shifted to Wucheng township marquis guarding Ye as northern gentleman.

sentences.zh: 五等建，封祝阿伯，累遷冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When five ranks were established enfeoffed Baron of Zhu'e progressively Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: Five-rank reform made him Zhu'e baron then champion general.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封濟南王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan created Jinan prince.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 二子：耽、緝。

translations.literal: Two sons: Dan and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Dan and Ji.

sentences.zh: 耽嗣立，徙為中山王。

translations.literal: Dan succeeded transferred Prince of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Dan moved the seat to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 是年薨，無子，緝繼。

translations.literal: Same year died without sons Ji continued.
translations.idiomatic: Dan died childless same year; Ji followed.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎以緝為建威將軍，與石熙等率眾距王浚，沒於陣，薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying appointed Ji bulwark general leading hosts with Shi Xi resisting Wang Jun perishing in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ying named Ji bulwark general alongside Shi Xi to stop Wang Jun; Ji died on the field.

sentences.zh: 無子，國除。

translations.literal: Having no sons state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Without heirs the principality ended.

sentences.zh: =曾孫勳=

translations.literal: Great-grandson Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson Xun.

sentences.zh: 後遂之曾孫勳字偉長，年十餘歲，湣帝末，長安陷，劉曜將令狐泥養為子。

translations.literal: Later Sui's great-grandson Xun courtesy Weichang age over ten at Emperor Min's end Chang'an fell Liu Yao general Linghu Ni raised him as son.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Ni adopted young Xun after Chang'an fell.

sentences.zh: 及壯，便弓馬，能左右射，，自關右還，自列云「是大長秋恂之玄孫，冠軍將軍濟南惠王遂之曾孫，略陽太守瓘之子」，遂拜謁者僕射，以勇聞。

translations.literal: Reaching adulthood skilled horse archery shooting both hands returning from west of the pass self-listed saying 'I am senior palace attendant Xun's great-great-grandson champion general Prince Hui of Jinan Sui's great-grandson governor of Lueyang Guan's son' thereupon appointed Herald Superintendent famed courage.
translations.idiomatic: Adult Xun claimed royal pedigree and won herald superintendent rank for valor.

sentences.zh: 庾翼之鎮襄陽，以梁州刺史援桓宣卒，請勳代之。

translations.literal: When Yu Yi garrisoned Xiangyang because the Liang Inspector's aide Huan Xuan died he requested Xun replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi at Xiangyang asked Xun to fill the Liang post vacated by aide Huan Xuan's death.

sentences.zh: 初屯西城，退守武當。

translations.literal: At first encamped western citadel withdrew guarding Wudang.
translations.idiomatic: He first garrisoned the west town then pulled back to Wudang.

sentences.zh: 時石季龍死，中國亂，雍州諸豪帥馳告勳。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Jilong died central plains chaotic Yongzhou magnates galloped informing Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's death unraveled the north; Yongzhou strongmen raced word to Sima Xun.

sentences.zh: 勳率眾出駱谷，壁於懸鉤，去長安二百里，遣部將劉煥攻長安，又拔賀城。

translations.literal: Xun led hosts exiting Luogu valley fortifying Xuāngou two hundred li from Chang'an dispatching subordinate Liu Huan attacking Chang'an again capturing Hecheng.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Luogu, camped near Chang'an, sent Liu Huan to raid the capital and took Hecheng.

sentences.zh: 於是關中皆殺季龍太守令長以應勳。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guanzhong altogether killed Shi Hu's governors magistrates and commandants responding to Xun.
translations.idiomatic: All Guanzhong slew Hu's officials to rally to Xun.

sentences.zh: 勳兵少，未能自固，復還梁州。

translations.literal: Xun's troops were few unable to secure himself returning again Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Too weak to hold ground he retreated to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永和中，張琚據隴東，遣使召勳，勳復入長安。

translations.literal: In Yonghe middle years Zhang Ju occupied Long east dispatching envoys summoning Xun; Xun again entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju's eastern Long grip drew Xun back into Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 初，京兆人杜洪以豪族陵琚，琚以勇俠侮洪，洪知勳憚琚兵強，因說勳曰；

translations.literal: At first Jingzhao man Du Hong by powerful clan oppressed Ju; Ju by bold fellowship insulted Hong; Hong knew Xun feared Ju's strong troops therefore persuaded Xun saying
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong and Zhang Ju feuded; Hong played on Xun's fear of Ju's strength:

sentences.zh: 「不殺張琚，關中非國家有也。

translations.literal: If you do not kill Zhang Ju Guanzhong will not be the state's possession.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Cut down Zhang Ju or lose Guanzhong.'

sentences.zh: 」勳乃偽請琚，於坐殺之。

translations.literal: Xun then falsely invited Ju killing him seated.
translations.idiomatic: Xun feasted Ju and slew him at table.

sentences.zh: 琚弟走池陽，合眾攻勳，頻戰不利，請和，歸梁州。

translations.literal: Ju's younger brother fled Chiyang gathering hosts attacking Xun frequent battles unfavorable requesting peace returning Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's brother rallied from Chiyang, fought Xun to stalemate, then sued for peace back in Liang.

sentences.zh: 後桓溫伐關中，命勳出子午道，而為苻雄所敗，退屯於女媧堡。

translations.literal: Later Huan Wen campaigned Guanzhong ordering Xun exit Ziwu road but was defeated by Fu Xiong withdrawing encamped at Nüwa fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's operation sent Xun up Ziwu until Fu Xiong broke him at Nüwa.

sentences.zh: 俄遷征虜將軍，監關中軍事，領西戎校尉，賜爵通吉亭侯。

translations.literal: Soon promoted general Who Subdues Captives supervising Guanzhong military affairs concurrent western tribes colonel enfeoffed Marquis of Tongji precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion brought subduing-captive rank, Guanzhong oversight, tribal colonel, and Tongji ting.

sentences.zh: 為政暴酷，至於治中別駕及州之豪右，言語忤意，即於坐梟斬之，或引弓自射。

translations.literal: His governance was violent-cruel reaching assistants regional aides and provincial magnates—speech offending intent meant immediate execution seated or drawing bow personally shooting.
translations.idiomatic: He executed aides and notables on whim, sometimes with his own bow.

sentences.zh: 西土患其凶虐。

translations.literal: Western lands suffered his fierce cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The west dreaded his savagery.

sentences.zh: 在州常懷據蜀，有僭偽之意。

translations.literal: In province he constantly harbored occupying Shu intent usurping pretension.
translations.idiomatic: He eyed Yi Province for a throne of his own.

sentences.zh: 桓溫聞之，務相綏懷，以其子康為漢中太守。

translations.literal: Huan Wen hearing this diligently soothed appointing his son Kang Hanzhong governor.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen placated him naming Kang Hanzhong shepherd.

sentences.zh: 勳逆謀已成，憚益州刺史周撫，未發。

translations.literal: Xun's rebellion scheme already formed feared Yi Inspector Zhou Fu not launching.
translations.idiomatic: Plot ready, he hesitated while Zhou Fu lived.
